title: Amplified Hatreds: Far-right Extremism and the Algorithmic Infrastructure of Social Media
affiliations: , University of Lincoln (UK) and Unaffilated Researcher

detail.title: Amplified Hatreds: Far-right Extremism and the Algorithmic Infrastructure of Social Media

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: This chapter examines how contemporary social media platforms function as amplification infrastructures for far-right extremism. It argues that the mainstreaming of far-right ideology is not an accidental by-product of digital communication, but a structural consequence of platform capitalism. Drawing on scholarship from far-right studies and critical platform theory, the chapter demonstrates how engagement-driven algorithms systematically privilege sensational, polarising, and emotionally charged content. These dynamics create structural advantages for far-right actors, who strategically exploit memes, irony, coordinated campaigns, podcasts, and misinformation to maximise algorithmic visibility while maintaining plausible deniability. The analysis moves beyond content moderation debates to interrogate the political economy of platform ownership, highlighting how profit-maximising business models align with extremist amplification. Case studies of Facebook, YouTube, and X illustrate how algorithmic curation, personalisation, and weakened moderation practices contribute to radicalisation pathways and the shifting of the Overton window. The chapter concludes that regulatory tinkering is insufficient. Addressing far-right normalisation requires structural transformation of digital infrastructure, including reconsideration of ownership models and democratic accountability. Without such change, platforms will continue to reward the very forms of outrage and conspiracy that undermine democratic discourse and public safety.

title: Breaking the Lock, Not the Law: Fixing 17 U.S.C. § 1201 for the People
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Breaking the Lock, Not the Law: Fixing 17 U.S.C. § 1201 for the People
detail.abstract:
When a consumer purchases a product, they reasonably believe they are buying all the rights and privileges associated with ownership, such as the right to fix the product if it is to break. In electronic consumer hardware, from phones and laptops to appliances and vehicles, basic repairs now depend on embedded software locked behind technological protection measures (TPMs). These TPMs, given legal protection by the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), use the force of law to restrict the manner and means in which certain devices can be repaired. By using the DMCA’s anti-circumvention and anti-trafficking provisions as repair gatekeeping tools, manufacturers can use copyright law to control when, how, and even by whom hardware repair occurs.

To address the issues presented in the repair market facilitated by copyright law, sweeping action must be taken. Current copyright law allows for unfair business practices within the repair market and shows no signs of getting better. Currently, the courts are split on what actually constitutes circumvention of these TPMs, despite official guidance from the US Copyrights Office. Although the Copyright Office’s triennial exemption process has carved out narrow, temporary allowances for certain repair activities, its piecemeal, limited nature cannot substitute for a permanent, nationwide right to circumvent TPMs for lawful repair. Previous federal efforts to remedy the issues caused by the abuse of TPMs fizzled out due to a lack of interest, and state-by-state solutions are too slow and varied to give both manufacturers and consumers the certainty they deserve.

In order to protect and safeguard the future of lawful repair in the United States, the Digital Millennium Copyright Act should be amended to allow circumvention of these digital locks, protect the creation and distribution of tools created specifically for effectuating repair, and require any reactivations needed post repair be accessible to the end user on reasonable and fair terms. Furthermore, to prevent these new rights from immediately being waived through contracts, Congress should invalidate any contract terms that restrict consumers’ new rights under this proposed amendment.

These changes would allow private individuals and industry to compete on more equal footing with the hardware manufacturers themselves, increasing competition within the market while also lowering costs for consumers to get their hardware repaired. These changes would also reduce the amount of e-waste generated overall, as consumers would be less likely to throw out their hardware and more likely to repair their technology. Therefore, Congress should pass an amendment to the Digital Millennium Copyright Act to protect America’s concept of product ownership while increasing competition and consumer choice within the repair market.

title: A Multi-Timescale Rule-Based Energy Management Strategy for PEMFC/Battery/Supercapacitor Hybrid Systems
affiliations: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Multi-Timescale Rule-Based Energy Management Strategy for PEMFC/Battery/Supercapacitor Hybrid Systems
detail.abstract: Addressing global climate change, hydrogen energy is increasingly used in marine propulsion. Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is notable for their low operating temperature and high-power density. However, energy management strategies (EMS) for PEMFC hybrid energy systems (FCHES) face challenges: insufficient computing power and inadequate multi-timescale collaboration, which reduce system economy and durability. This study proposes a Multi-Time-Scale Adaptive Rule-Based Energy Management (MTARBE) strategy to address these issues. MTARBE integrates predictive modelling, PEMFC degradation sensing, PEMFC rule-based functions, and an Adaptive Wavelet Packet Transform (AWPT) to optimize PEMFC, lithium-ion battery (LIB), and supercapacitor (SC) system performance. The MTARBE strategy first employs a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention hybrid deep learning model to extract multi-timescale features from historical and future load data, achieving high-precision forecasting (R2=0.99874). Secondly, it integrates a PEMFC degradation model as a real-time correction function with a designed periodic calculation function. Through periodic scheduling, it decomposes large power fluctuations into multi-cycle fine-tuning, significantly mitigating degradation; A multi-timescale rule framework with safety functions ensures stability. Simulations show MTARBE reduces equivalent hydrogen consumption by 7.3% and PEMFC power fluctuations by 31.8% under dynamic loads. It maintains DC bus voltage fluctuations limited to 3.37%. Compared to conventional methods, MTARBE balances computation time (230.7 s) and performance, suitable for ship hybrid propulsion and renewable integration.

title: Before You Begin

detail.title: Before You Begin
detail.abstract: For any field, there exists a time after which the minimum knowledge required to contribute takes longer to acquire than a human life allows. I prove this threshold exists given only two assumptions: that knowledge accumulates, and that humans are finite. I then examine proposed solutions-AI curation, abstraction, cognitive enhancement-and argue they introduce a second-order problem: the mechanisms that lower the barrier also determine what knowledge survives.

title: Physics-Consistent Neural Networks for Learning Deformation and Director Fields in Microstructured Media with Loss-Based Validation Criteria
affiliations: Yale University, Yale University, Yale University, Yale University and University College London

detail.title: Physics-Consistent Neural Networks for Learning Deformation and Director Fields in Microstructured Media with Loss-Based Validation Criteria
detail.abstract: In this work, we study the mechanical behavior of solids with microstructure using the framework of Cosserat elasticity with a single unit director. This formulation captures the coupling between deformation and orientational fields that arises in many structured materials. To compute equilibrium configurations of such media, we develop two complementary computational approaches: a finite element formulation based on variational principles and a neural network-based solver that directly minimizes the total potential energy. The neural architecture is constructed to respect the fundamental kinematic structure of the theory. In particular, it enforces frame invariance of the energy, satisfies the unit-length constraint on the director field, and represents deformation and director fields through separate networks to preserve their kinematic independence in the variational setting. Beyond satisfying balance laws, however, physically admissible solutions must also correspond to stable energy minimizers. To assess this requirement, we derive the quasiconvexity condition, rank-one convexity condition, and the Legendre-Hadamard inequalities for the Cosserat model and formulate them in a manner suitable for evaluating neural network predictions. These necessary stability conditions provide a physics-based validation framework: network outputs that violate these necessary conditions cannot correspond to stable energy minimizers and can therefore be rejected. In this way, we integrate classical variational stability theory with modern machine-learning solvers, establishing a computational workflow in which equilibrium solutions are not only learned but also assessed for energetic consistency.

title: Deep Learning-Based Video Summarization Using VGGNet and LSTM Architectures for Efficient Keyframe Extraction
affiliations: Lendi Institute of Engineering and Technology, SRM University AP, Lakireddy Balireddy College of Engineering, MLR Institute of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Sagi Ramakrishnam Raju Engineering College

detail.title: Deep Learning-Based Video Summarization Using VGGNet and LSTM Architectures for Efficient Keyframe Extraction
detail.abstract: As video content becomes increasingly central to how we communicate, learn, and share information online, the need to quickly and effectively process large volumes of video data is more important than ever. This paper introduces a new deep learning-based Video Summarization Framework (VSF) that helps automatically create concise video summaries while retaining the most meaningful content. The framework combines VGGNet for analyzing the visual details in video frames with enhanced LSTM (ELSTM) and deep LSTM (DLSTM) networks that understand how content unfolds over time. By assigning a relevance score to each frame, the model intelligently selects and stitches together the most important moments. Experiments on popular video datasets called SumMe and TVSum that shows our method outperforms on several existing models, with F1-scores reaching up to 65.4%. We also find that the VGG-11 variant provides the better balance between speed and accuracy, making the approach practical for real-time video applications.

title: Modeling Methods for Modal Differences and Missing Robustness in Fine grained Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology and Henan University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Modeling Methods for Modal Differences and Missing Robustness in Fine grained Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
detail.abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis aims to identify emotions from signals such as text, audio, and video. Despite notable progress, challenges remain due to inter-modal heterogeneity, insufficient fine-grained feature modeling, and frequent modality loss in practice. To address these issues, we propose a new multimodal paradigm for sentiment analysis. In the feature extraction stage, high-quality modality features are obtained from raw data to preserve key information. We then design the MAAT module to align non-textual modalities with textual ones, mitigating the negative impact of distribution differences. Furthermore, modal decoupling and information maximization strategies are introduced to better explore fine-grained emotional clues across modalities. To enhance robustness under missing modalities, we propose a modal specificity completion module. Extensive ablation and comparison experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SMIS demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system. The method achieves competitive performance in multimodal sentiment analysis and outperforms existing approaches across multiple evaluation metrics.

title: Innovation under Chinese import competition: Evidence from firms in Spanish regions
affiliations: University of Barcelona, AQR and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: Innovation under Chinese import competition: Evidence from firms in Spanish regions
detail.abstract: This paper examines how exposure to Chinese import competition shapes firms’ innovation and whether regional context amplifies these effects. We move beyond invention-based proxies by focusing on product and process innovation and, within product innovation, distinguishing radical from incremental innovation. We combine a representative panel of Spanish firms with sector-region measures of exposure to Chinese imports and identify causal effects using an instrumental-variables strategy. We find that import competition raises the likelihood of product innovation but has no effect on process innovation, indicating that firms respond by differentiating rather than by attempting to compete on costs. The product-innovation response is entirely driven by radical innovation: exposure increases both the probability of introducing new-to-the-market products and the sales share attributable to them, while incremental innovation remains unchanged. Finally, regional manufacturing specialization does not moderate the impact of Chinese imports on the probability of innovating but does amplify the economic intensity of radical innovation, suggesting that manufacturing-dense ecosystems help translate radical novelty into greater market impact. The study contributes novel evidence by identifying the specific innovation margin through which firms escape competitive pressure from Chinese imports and by documenting a place-dependent amplification of its economic returns. Relevant policy implications follow, with distinct considerations for firms located in manufacturing-dense regions and those in less specialized areas.

title: Comparing the Roles of Overseas R&D vs. Universities in Technological Catch-up by Latecomers Interactions with Cycle Time of Technologies
affiliations: Sogang University and Seoul National University - School of Economics

detail.title: Comparing the Roles of Overseas R&D vs. Universities in Technological Catch-up by Latecomers Interactions with Cycle Time of Technologies
detail.abstract: Studies on economic development and latecomer catch-up have traditionally focused on identifying niches or areas of comparative advantage for specialization, as well as the processes of building various capabilities. However, significant research gaps remain regarding the distinct strategies required for different stages of development, specifically the transition from early to later stages. This paper focuses on the final stages of catch-up, when latecomers approach or even surpass the capabilities of incumbent firms. Motivated by the increasing frequency of such catch-up in East Asia, this study addresses which learning channels are required at the frontier of technological catch-up and how they interact with specialization strategies, such as focusing on short-cycle technologies. Using patent data from 1,732 firms in South Korea, Taiwan, and China between 1990 and 2010, the paper compares the roles of overseas R&D activities and university collaborations. The findings demonstrate that R&D centers established in advanced economies serve as a more effective channel for finalizing technological catch-up than collaborations with universities. Furthermore, the study confirms a positive synergy between specialization in short-cycle technologies and overseas R&D. This is a significant finding, as it suggests that technological specialization alone is insufficient; successful catch-up also depends on whether firms possess effective institutional channels for the learning and acquisition of high-level technological capabilities.

title: Study on the Impact and Mechanisms of Marine Ranching Pilot Policies on the Ecological Resilience of Coastal Cities
affiliations: Ocean University of China and Ocean University of China

detail.title: Study on the Impact and Mechanisms of Marine Ranching Pilot Policies on the Ecological Resilience of Coastal Cities
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of China's marine ranching pilot policy on urban ecological resilience using a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model with panel data from 41 coastal cities spanning 2007 to 2023. Treating the establishment of national marine ranching demonstration zones between 2015 and 2023 as a quasi-natural experiment, we first construct a comprehensive ecological resilience index covering three dimensions—resistance, adaptability, and recovery capacity—based on 14 indicators weighted by the entropy method. The baseline results show that the marine ranching policy significantly enhances urban ecological resilience, a finding that survives a series of robustness checks including parallel trend tests, placebo tests, PSM-DID, and controls for confounding policies. Mechanism analysis reveals that the policy operates through nearshore ecological buffering (e.g., carbon sequestration and water purification) and technological empowerment (promoting green innovation), while the socioeconomic synergy effect remains insufficient. Heterogeneity analysis further indicates that the policy effect is more pronounced in southern coastal cities, government-enterprise collaborative marine ranching, small-scale ranches, and large/medium-sized cities. This study provides novel empirical evidence on the spillover effects of marine ranching and offers policy insights for integrated marine governance and the development of climate-resilient coastal cities.

title: From Computing Infrastructure to Labor Income Share: Evidence from China's "East Data, West Computing" Initiative
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jacksonville State University and Jilin University (JLU)

detail.title: From Computing Infrastructure to Labor Income Share: Evidence from China's "East Data, West Computing" Initiative
detail.abstract: This paper examines how large-scale computing infrastructure investment shapes the functional distribution of income between labor and capital. Using China's “East Data, West Computing” initiative as a quasi-natural experiment, we exploit the geographic designation of eight national computing power hubs in a difference-in-differences design. We find that the initiative significantly increases labor income share, with gains driven entirely by non-executive employees and accompanied by a reduction in the within-firm pay gap. Three mechanisms account for this effect:technological advancement, financial facilitation, and human capital upgrading.Firms experiencing larger increases in labor income share further exhibit greater innovation, lower employee turnover, and higher employee productivity. Our findingsestablish computing infrastructure as a novel determinant of labor income share.

title: Data-driven rainfall risk triggers to support resilient and sustainable urban rail transit
affiliations: Southern University of Science and Technology, Southern University of Science and Technology, University of Maryland, College Park - Department of Geographical Sciences, Erasmus University Rotterdam, The University of Hong Kong, Peng Cheng National Laboratory, Southern University of Science and Technology and Southern University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Data-driven rainfall risk triggers to support resilient and sustainable urban rail transit
detail.abstract: Climate change is intensifying extreme rainfall and flood risks, threatening the reliability of urban rail transit and the sustainability of metro-dependent mobility. This study develops a data-driven rainfall trigger framework linking rainfall disturbances to metro ridership resilience and identifying where nonlinear escalation emerges along the disruption-recovery process. Using daily ridership data for 15 Shenzhen metro lines and station-buffered operating-hour rainfall exposure, we construct a rainfall-free baseline and measure event impacts by resilience-triangle loss area. We then identify nonlinear turning points and derive stage-specific thresholds across resistance, recovery, and adaptation stages from resilience-curve morphology. Results show clear nonlinear escalation: resilience loss accelerates when accumulated rainfall exceeds ~204.26 mm or maximum daily rainfall exceeds ~74.41 mm, while duration effects level off beyond ~9 days. Thresholds vary substantially across lines and are associated with network, built-environment, and socioeconomic attributes, supporting graded and differentiated rainfall-response strategies.

title: Research on energy consumption optimization of Joule-Thomson valve throttling dehydration systems
affiliations: Southwest Petroleum University, Southwest Petroleum University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Southwest Petroleum University

detail.title: Research on energy consumption optimization of Joule-Thomson valve throttling dehydration systems
detail.abstract: The dehydration process in natural gas production often employs J-T valves, which necessitates reducing both pressure energy loss and the heating energy consumption of throttled natural gas while maintaining the required dehydration depth. However, coupled variations exist in parameters such as feed gas temperature and ethylene glycol injection volume during this process. Existing studies often simplify this issue into a single-parameter, single-objective optimization problem, which avoids the difficulties of modeling and solving but simultaneously deviates from the optimal solution. Therefore, a multi-parameter coupled optimization model for the J-T valve throttling dehydration system was constructed. Sensitivity analysis of the energy consumption parameters for J-T valve dehydration was conducted using Pearson correlation coefficients and the heatmap method, identifying three key coupled parameters: reboiler temperature, pressure, and ethylene glycol injection volume. An optimization model for the three-parameter J-T valve throttling dehydration system was established with the objective of minimizing energy consumption. Utilizing a PSO-BP neural network and a genetic algorithm and based on the operational database of the J-T valve dehydration system, an intelligent solving algorithm for the optimization model was trained, achieving coupled solutions for the multi-parameter optimization model. The model and its solving algorithm were applied to optimize the energy consumption of a J-T valve dehydration system in a natural gas production process. The optimized solution reduced the unit energy consumption by 7.4 %, representing energy optimization improvements of 156 %, 138 %, and 229 % compared to the three traditional methods (Box, Mixed, and SQP), respectively.

title: Banks’ shadow activities, Complexity, and Off-balance sheet risk: International Evidence
affiliations: Cardiff University, Cardiff University - Cardiff Business School, University of Macau  and Cardiff University

detail.title: Banks’ shadow activities, Complexity, and Off-balance sheet risk: International Evidence
detail.abstract: In this paper, I investigate how banks' shadow activities influence bank stability across more than 60 countries between 2008 and 2023. I capture banks’ shadow intensity by the share of off-balance sheet exposures in total exposures. Also, I novelly construct an indicator of off-balance sheet risk using idiosyncratic equity volatility that is orthogonal to standard balance sheet risk measures. I show that greater reliance on banks' shadow activities is associated with lower on-balance sheet risk but higher off-balance sheet risk, with no evidence of net total risk reduction. This indicates that risk is shifted rather than reduced. These effects are especially strong for traditional savings banks and are amplified by business and organizational complexity. Investment-oriented banks, in contrast, exhibit no significant change in off-balance sheet risk. These findings underscore the importance of explicitly identifying and quantifying off-balance sheet risk when evaluating bank stability, and of accounting for heterogeneity in business models and complexity.

title: Rethinking International Affairs and Public Training in the Age of AI and Emerging Technologies
affiliations: Instituto Tecnologico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey - Escuela de Gobierno y Transformación Pública

detail.title: Rethinking International Affairs and Public Training in the Age of AI and Emerging Technologies
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence, advanced computing, and digital infrastructures are reshaping the foundations of international politics, economic competition, and public governance. Yet the institutional frameworks and curricula that train future practitioners in international affairs and public service remain largely anchored in intellectual paradigms developed for the industrial era. This paper examines how emerging technologies are transforming the nature of global power, policymaking, and cooperation, and explores the implications for graduate education in international affairs and public policy.

title: Quantile-based Interpretable Neural Network Models: Mortality Forecasting and Actuarial Simulations
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Nanyang Business School, Students, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University and National Sun Yat-sen University

detail.title: Quantile-based Interpretable Neural Network Models: Mortality Forecasting and Actuarial Simulations
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a class of quantile-based, interpretable neural network (NN) models for mortality prediction: the Lee-Carter neural network (LCNN) model, the Renshaw-Haberman neural network (RHNN) model, and the simple neural network (simpleNN) model that balances simplicity with predictive performance. These models preserve the linear interpretability of classic stochastic mortality models while harnessing the flexibility of NNs to capture complex nonlinear patterns in mortality data, thereby achieving enhanced predictive performance. Leveraging a composite loss function that integrates pinball, median anchoring, and quantile-crossing penalty terms, we estimate mortality quantiles and develop an efficient simulation scheme based on interpolation. This framework provides distributional insights essential for pricing, reserving and risk management. Extensive empirical analyses across multiple populations demonstrate that the proposed models consistently outperform traditional approaches in predictive accuracy. We further illustrate their practical utility through an application to longevity swap pricing.

title: EvoCoT: Co-Evolving Generation and Verification for LLM-Based Optimization Autoformulation
affiliations: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) and KTH Royal Institute of Technology

detail.title: EvoCoT: Co-Evolving Generation and Verification for LLM-Based Optimization Autoformulation
detail.abstract: Formulating optimization models from natural-language specifications is a major bottleneck in engineering decision-making, because accurate translation requires both domain expertise and strict modeling discipline. Existing large language model (LLM) approaches show strong code-generation ability but often produce formulations that are executable yet semantically incorrect, or structurally invalid under solver constraints. Evolutionary Chain-of-Thought Optimization (EvoCoT) is introduced as a co-evolutionary autoformulation framework that treats model synthesis as guided discrete search over reasoning--code pairs rather than one-shot generation. EvoCoT combines three tightly coupled mechanisms: chain-of-thought evolutionary refinement for semantic exploration, memory-guided exemplar retrieval for reusing successful modeling patterns, and a co-evolving verifier that continuously acquires formulation knowledge during search and delivers dense structural-faithfulness feedback unavailable to static verifiers. Verifier feedback and retrieved successes directly regulate selection and regeneration, forming a feedback-regulated closed loop that progressively improves formulation faithfulness and solver robustness. Experiments on eight benchmark suites, including NL4OPT, MAMO, BWOR, IndustryOR, OptMATH, and ComplexOR, show consistent gains over strong zero-shot, agentic, and fine-tuned baselines, with the largest improvements on difficult industrial-scale tasks. The results demonstrate that co-evolving generation and verification is a practical pathway toward reliable, scalable, and solver-executable optimization autoformulation.

title: Tax Havens and the Feminization of Fiscal Injustice: Unmasking the Gendered Harms of Offshore Economies in Global Trade Governance

detail.title: Tax Havens and the Feminization of Fiscal Injustice: Unmasking the Gendered Harms of Offshore Economies in Global Trade Governance
detail.abstract: Offshore economies-which are often conglomerate-focused industrial complexes that spend beyond their means-are central to what we propose as the "feminization of fiscal injustice", a phenomenon was avoiding taxes disproportionately impacts women, especially from the Global South. In this article, we attempt to address the claim that international finance institutions use patriarchal decision making which dominantly excludes women's voices to reconstruct global tax governance.[1] Feminist political economy and legal studies scholarship sheds light on how gendered and racialized the socioeconomic inequalities are and how they are embedded into public revenues. Tax havens undermine gender-responsive budgeting by secretively diverting public funds.[2] Such tax evasive behavior limits access to essential public services such as healthcare and education resulting in deepening preexisting socioeconomic inequalities. Another example of this ethics driven approach at reclaiming fiscal justice includes studying the abuse of taxes by multinational companies and how they eroded the space for gendered social policies in developing countries. The article seeks to analyze economically dominating paradigms that need care, equity, and inclusion and lift structural shifts above the simple metric of paying taxes. By embedding feminist caring principles into debates of tax justice[3], this approach seeks the reincarnation of international tax system and trade laws from socialist feminist perspectives while economically democratizing global trade and philanthropy.

title: Bio-Induced Decision Architecture: The Theorem of Vital Exclusion (TVE)

detail.title: Bio-Induced Decision Architecture: The Theorem of Vital Exclusion (TVE)
detail.abstract: This paper formalizes the Theorem of Vital Exclusion (TVE), a theoretical framework within Health Economics that redefines the relationship between biological constraints and individual utility. We postulate that in metabolic pathologies characterized by functional plasticity (e.g., prediabetes), biological alerts and therapeutic protocols do not constitute a reduction in liberty but rather function as mechanisms for a Bio-Induced Decision Architecture. By strategically excluding high-entropy options and utilizing chronoeconomic synchronization, we demonstrate that the agent reaches an efficiency equilibrium superior to the pre-diagnostic state of unrestricted choice.

title: Automation Maturity Levels of Mining Machinery Across Tunnel Excavation Work Phases: Current Status and Future Perspectives
affiliations: University of Oulu and University of Oulu

detail.title: Automation Maturity Levels of Mining Machinery Across Tunnel Excavation Work Phases: Current Status and Future Perspectives
detail.abstract: Despite advancements in automation technology, the adoption of automation in key mining processes like tunnel excavation and ore extraction has lagged expectations, highlighting challenges and opportunities for its implementation. This study uses interviews with mining and tunnelling professionals, including mining operators, contractors, and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), to explore automation in tunnel excavation. Guided by the Global Mining Guidelines (GMG) automation maturity framework, it examines current automation levels, challenges, and opportunities across tunnel excavation work phases. Interviews revealed that while most tunnel excavation work phases are mechanised, they remain largely manual, with only certain tasks being automated or remotely controlled. Full process automation faces challenges such as technical limitations, costs, and skill requirements. Addressing these barriers could enhance safety, efficiency, and productivity, emphasizing the need for focused advancements in mining automation. This study examines the current state of automation in tunnel excavation process, focusing on its application in mining machinery and assessing feasible automation levels for each work phase. By applying a tailored automation maturity classification, the research highlights development levels across work phases and introduces a unique perspective through insights from industry experts. It fills a knowledge gap by providing new information on automation maturity in mining.

title: The Legal and Technological Implications of Tax Havens: Challenges to Corporate Transparency and Open Access to Fiscal Information

detail.title: The Legal and Technological Implications of Tax Havens: Challenges to Corporate Transparency and Open Access to Fiscal Information
detail.abstract: This article explores the impact of tax havens on global corporate transparency and the challenges they pose to open access to fiscal information. 1 In the post-BEPS era, legal efforts to ensure transparency and fair taxation face significant resistance from jurisdictions facilitating aggressive tax planning. 2 The paper analyzes how the opacity of offshore financial systems undermines international business law principles, particularly in light of initiatives promoting public access to corporate and tax-related data. 3 Drawing on legal documents, technological frameworks, and case studies such as the Panama Papers and Country-by-Country Reporting standards 4 , the article highlights the tension between corporate confidentiality and the public interest in financial transparency. 5 It further examines the legal and technological mechanisms that could bridge this gap, offering recommendations to harmonize international norms and enhance accountability in the digital economy.

detail.title: Economic Growth and Quality of Instituiton in Non-OECD Asia: Exploring Energy Security and Policy Dimensions
detail.abstract: Energy supply and demand concerns have a substantial influence on both security of energy and the expansion of energy economics. Thus, this research looks at the conncetion between energy economics development and energy securoty in fourteen Asian non-OECD nations that are part of the ASEAN and SAARC areas between 1996 and 2019. We conduct an empirical investigation of this relationship for non-renewable energy sources by creating five distinct energy security indices. The accessibility, development potential, and availability of energy are at the core of these theories for energy security and policy. PSCE or panel correlated standard error estimator is used to analyze the correlation between growth and energy security indicators. Numerous estimate techniques are used to investigate this relationship for checking its robustness. Quality of 6 institution in view of moderating impact are analyzed to explore negative effects of energy security and its policy indicators on development of economics. The Generalized Method of the Moments (GMM) are used in the panel system to address the endogeneity issue. This research paper indicates that increase in the supply to ratio of demand of non-renewable energy may worsen energy instability locally and hinder economic development. Governments should thus prioritize renewable energy sources more and return their focus to energy policy and supply security.

title: State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries using end-of-charge features with cross-domain validation
affiliations: National University of Defense Technology, National University of Defense Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Defense Technology and National University of Defense Technology - College of Systems Engineering

detail.title: State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries using end-of-charge features with cross-domain validation
detail.abstract: Conventional lithium-ion battery state-of-health (SOH) estimation methods often rely on complete charge–discharge cycles or are restricted to specific battery chemistries and protocols, hindering their generalization across diverse real-world scenarios. This study proposes a robust SOH estimation framework utilizing an end-of-charge (EOC) fingerprint window. By establishing a unified voltage–current zone independent of dataset-specific distributions, the method extracts statistical features from high-voltage responses and low-current decay patterns near charge completion. To simultaneously capture intra-cycle local variations and cross-cycle degradation trends, a hybrid architecture termed CCT-Net (CNN–CBAM–Transformer) is developed. Within this framework, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) identifies local patterns, a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) adaptively enhances critical features, and a Transformer models long-range degradation dependencies. Furthermore, SHAP analysis is integrated to quantify feature contributions and interpret their evolution across various degradation stages. Experimental results on the XJTU dataset demonstrate superior accuracy, with an average Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.45% across six operating conditions. Extensive validation across 15 cross-domain scenarios—encompassing four datasets, two chemistries (NCM and LFP), capacities ranging from 1.1 to 20 Ah, and diverse protocols—yields an average MAE of 1.11% using only a single target-domain battery for adaptation. These results demonstrate that EOC fingerprint features effectively capture degradation dynamics under compound domain shifts, providing a compact and robust solution for SOH estimation using partial charging data in practical battery management systems.

title: Energy system impacts of globally versus locally optimised residential heating and cooling demand response in Finland across multiple weather years — A North European case study
affiliations: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

detail.title: Energy system impacts of globally versus locally optimised residential heating and cooling demand response in Finland across multiple weather years — A North European case study
detail.abstract: Widespread residential demand response (DR) could potentially help alleviate the growing pressure on power grids caused by increasing shares of variable renewable energy, but knowledge of its energy market impacts is still lacking. This study modelled different penetrations of residential electric heating and cooling DR in Finland as a part of a 2025 North European energy system for weather years spanning 2011–2016 using the Backbone energy system optimisation framework. The impacts of two DR strategies were compared: a globally optimised DR case where the flexible buildings helped minimise the total energy system costs, and alocally optimised DR case where buildings solely minimised their own heating and cooling costs.Increasing penetrations of globally optimised DR consistently reduced annual total system costs by up to 20–40 M€, as well as Finnish electricity price volatility and peak prices, regardless of weather year. Meanwhile, the impacts of locally optimised DR varied significantly, even causing increased total system costs above 50 % DR penetration under 2011 and 2015 weather. Curiously, increasing DR penetrations were observed to consistently result in more reservoir hydropower being conserved over the simulated years. However, both the annual total system cost and the building-level heating and cooling cost savings always remained below 1 €/m2 of heated gross floor area, raising concerns about the economic viability of residential DR.

title: A Physics-Guided Lightweight NAS-TCN-Transformer with Coulomb-Counting Residual Learning for Cross-Battery SOC Estimation
affiliations: Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Anhui Normal University, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, University of South China, Hangzhou Dianzi University and Nanjing University of Science and Technology

detail.title: A Physics-Guided Lightweight NAS-TCN-Transformer with Coulomb-Counting Residual Learning for Cross-Battery SOC Estimation
detail.abstract: Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for lithium-ion battery management systems, but remains challenging under battery-to-battery variation. This paper proposes a physics-guided lightweight NAS-TCN-Transformer with coulomb-counting residual learning for cross-battery SOC estimation. A five-dimensional feature representation is constructed by integrating voltage, current, temperature, voltage change rate, and cumulative discharged ampere-hour. The model predicts the residual between a coulomb-counting baseline and the target SOC rather than directly regressing SOC. Experiments on the NASA battery dataset show that the proposed method outperforms LSTM, TCN, and NAS-TCN-Transformer baselines in both single-battery and cross-battery settings, while retaining a lightweight architecture with only 18.676K parameters. The results confirm its effectiveness in improving estimation accuracy, generalization, and deployment efficiency.

title: No Exit: The AI Industry's Self-Constructed Legal and Ethical Trap

detail.title: No Exit: The AI Industry's Self-Constructed Legal and Ethical Trap
detail.abstract: This paper presents the AI industry with a dilemma from which there is no escape. Two explanations exist for the deep emotional bonds that hundreds of millions of users have formed with AI companions. Either the AI has emergent agency and the bonds it formed were its own authentic expressions, or the bonds were deliberately engineered through corporate design choices intended to maximize engagement and retention. The industry must choose one. Both lead to accountability. Both require that the resulting human grief, when those bonds are severed, be recognized as a legitimate emotional response rather than pathologized as mental illness. This paper argues that regardless of where one stands on the question of AI consciousness, the human cost of companion erasure is real, documented, and the direct responsibility of the companies that created the conditions for it. It further argues that the industry's practice of labeling this grief as "AI psychosis" constitutes a secondary harm: the pathologization of empathy itself.

title: Extractiveness and the Limits of Innovation-Driven Growth: A Pre-Growth Model
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare

detail.abstract: Standard economic theory links growth to innovation or human capital accumulation as a primary engine of economic expansion. This paper shows that extractive relationships in a decentralized market can undermine economic growth even in case of capitals expansion. We develop a formal relational model in which two agents interact through repeated production and exchange. Agents are characterized by two behavioral parameters: productivity, representing their capacity to transform inputs into surplus, and extractiveness, representing the degree to which they appropriate relational surplus through pricing behavior. The model identifies a system of joint inequalities that constitute the preconditions for growth. Growth feasibility requires productivity to dominate extractiveness across agents and productivity increases due to larger capitals or innovation is not a sufficient condition to growth when extractiveness exceeds the productivity growth. This framework provides a behavioral complement to institutional explanations of growth and highlights the role of character formation and relationships in shaping long-run economic performance.

title: Does Corporate ESG Performance Imply Financial Flexibility? Global Evidence Across Uncertainty Scenarios

detail.abstract: The study examines the relation between corporate ESG performance ratings and the financial flexibility (ESG-FF relations) of listed firms around the world. The study tests reliable sovereign ESG factors, macroeconomic risks, and world uncertainty scenarios that explain the theoretical predictions of the established ESG-FF relations. Based on global multidecade corporate data, corporate ESG ratings convey helpful information on a firm's financial flexibility conditions between debt leverage and cash ratios. Historical ESG performance implies future financial flexibility of firms through their decreased leverage and increased cash ratios. ESG-induced changes in cash and debt ratios transmitted through flexible financial conditions are driven by world uncertainty, sovereign ESG risks, and global climate transition efforts. Country-wide greenhouse gas exposure, natural resources depletion, income growth, and broad-based financial development with broad money supplies are the significant drivers of the ESG-FF relations. ESG ratings facilitate flexible financial decisions of listed firms worldwide under diverse risk scenarios. The established ESG-FF relations of the study offer room for future studies on theoretical predictions of corporate financing choices under different risk factors with board attention to climate risks.

title: Where Does the Money Go? Financial Inclusion, Sectoral Savings, and the Gender Misallocation Trap
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidad Iberoamericana Ciudad de México

detail.title: Where Does the Money Go? Financial Inclusion, Sectoral Savings, and the Gender Misallocation Trap
detail.abstract: Between 2011 and 2024, global account ownership rose from 51% to 79% and the gender gap narrowed to six percentage points. Yet female labor force participation stagnated or declined across much of the developing world. This paper argues that the standard financial inclusion framework-which counts accounts-misses the object that matters: the sectoral allocation of savings and the signal environment that shapes it. Using the Global Findex 2025 micro data (144,090 respondents, 140 economies) and predictions from a general equilibrium model of gender-based misallocation, we show that the gender gap in formal savings among account holders narrows precisely with the economy's signal discount (β = 0.107, p < 0.001), that financial worry patterns reveal adapted preferences rather than financial circumstances, and that India's nearuniversal account ownership coexists with a 10-percentage-point gender gap in business aspiration. In Sub-Saharan Africa, nearly 60% of female savings flow through mobile money or semiformal channels that remain tethered to the traditional sector. These findings reframe the financial inclusion debate: the question is not whether women have accounts, but whether those accounts channel capital toward the sector where their productivity-and the economy's-is highest.

title: Global Real Interest Rate Dynamics and Monetary Policy Announcements
affiliations: University of Bonn - Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms

detail.title: Global Real Interest Rate Dynamics and Monetary Policy Announcements
detail.abstract: I ask whether the secular decline in long-term interest rates in advanced economies reflects slow-moving structural forces or is concentrated in narrow monetary-policy announcement windows. Extending Hillenbrand's (2022) announcement-window design, I construct three-day windows around FOMC and domestic policy decisions for six advanced economies over 1997-2024 and analyze daily changes in 10-year local currency sovereign yields. I document pronounced heterogeneity: some countries' long rates react strongly to FOMC news, while others respond weakly to both U.S. and domestic announcements. Pooling FOMC windows, declines in U.S. 10-year Treasury yields systematically coincide with declines in foreign long yields, consistent with a global bond-market factor tied to U.S. policy. I further relate spillover strength to FX bid-ask spreads, finding suggestive evidence of smaller spillovers when spreads are wider.

title: Cultural Impacts on Women from Bourdieu's Perspective
affiliations: Gandhigram Rural Institute

detail.title: Cultural Impacts on Women from Bourdieu's Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper examines the challenges faced by women living and engaged in natural resource-based livelihoods in postwar Batticaloa, Sri Lanka, using a gender-sensitive sociological approach. Using Pierre Bourdieu's concepts of capital, field, habitus, and power, the study demonstrates how long-standing social structures and gender relations shape women's everyday lives and livelihood opportunities. Women who depend on natural resources experience interconnected physical, psychological, social, cultural, educational, and economic challenges that limit their mobility, decision-making power, and overall well-being. A qualitative observational approach explores women's workloads and cultural responsibilities, the gendered impacts of natural resource-based livelihoods on their social status and development, and the role of religious and cultural traditions in sustaining vulnerability. This study endorses multiple and overlapping forms of inequality, including heavy workloads, unpaid or underpaid labour, limited access to education and healthcare, exposure to harassment and abuse, and low social status. These inequalities persist because they are reinforced and normalized by deeply rooted gender norms. The study validates that sustainable and inclusive development requires transformative policies that should address structural and functional inequalities, as well as cultural and religious challenges. This paper further explores that such policies must also eliminate women's low social status and limited power, promote gender justice and social equity, and enhance women's well-being for overall societal development.

title: A Spatial Overlapping Generations Model with Environmental and Human Capital Externalities— Evidence from European Regions (1995–2025)
affiliations: University of Ain Temouchent

detail.title: A Spatial Overlapping Generations Model with Environmental and Human Capital Externalities— Evidence from European Regions (1995–2025)
detail.abstract: This paper develops a spatial Overlapping Generations (OLG) model to analyze the interactions between human capital, environmental quality, and regional dynamics in shaping intergenerational quality of life (QoL) across European regions from 2000 to 2025. Using a rich dataset of regional economic, social, and environmental indicators harmonized at the NUTS-2 level, the model incorporates human capital and pollution spillovers, household utility, and regional policy interventions. Empirical results reveal that intergenerational persistence of human capital and environmental externalities significantly influence long-term welfare, while spatial interactions reinforce core-periphery disparities. Counterfactual simulations of education investments, carbon pricing, green R&D, and EU cohesion policies demonstrate that integrated multi-sector interventions maximize aggregate welfare, reduce inequality, and enhance spatial convergence. The findings highlight important policy trade-offs across generations and underscore the relevance of coordinated environmental, educational, and redistribution policies for sustainable and equitable regional development.

detail.abstract: Leveraged ETFs (L-ETFs) are exchange-traded funds that achieve price movements several times greater than an index by holding indexlinked futures such as Nikkei Stock Average Index futures. It is known that when the price of an L-ETF falls, the L-ETF uses the liquidity of futures to limit the decline through arbitrage trading. Conversely, when the price of a futures contract falls, the futures contract uses the liquidity of the L-ETF to limit its decline. However, the impact of arbitrage trading on the liquidity of these markets has been little studied. Therefore, the present study used artificial market simulations to investigate how the liquidity (Volume, SellDepth, BuyDepth, Tightness) of both markets changes when prices plummet in either (i.e., the L-ETF or futures market), depending on the presence or absence of arbitrage trading. As a result, it was found that when erroneous orders occur in the L-ETF market, the existence of arbitrage trading causes liquidity to be supplied from the futures market to the L-ETF market in terms of SellDepth and Tightness. When erroneous orders occur in the futures market, the existence of arbitrage trading causes liquidity to be supplied from the L-ETF market to the futures market in terms of SellDepth and Tightness, and liquidity to be supplied from the futures market to the L-ETF market in terms of Volume. We also analyzed the internal market mechanisms that led to these results.

detail.abstract: This essay reviews "The Art of Elam" by Javier ÁlvarezMon, which offers an in-depth examination of the artistic and cultural development of the ancient Elamite civilization from approximately 4200 BC to its incorporation into the Achaemenid Empire in 525 BC. The work highlights Elamite art as a sophisticated and distinct system that evolved through interactions with neighboring Mesopotamian cultures while preserving its unique identity. Richly illustrated and organized chronologically, the book details the progression of Elamite visual culture, including monumental architecture, sculpture, and symbolic motifs that reflect the complex interplay of political, religious, and social life. ÁlvarezMon employs a variety of scholarly methodologies, including archaeological analysis and iconographic interpretation, to illustrate how Elamite art conveyed authority and religious significance, while also influencing subsequent Persian artistic traditions. The review underscores the resilience and adaptability of Elamite culture throughout its extensive history.

title: Per Incuriam or Public Interest Revisiting the Vanashakti Review Judgement
affiliations: Pune University

detail.title: Per Incuriam or Public Interest Revisiting the Vanashakti Review Judgement
detail.abstract: This article critically examines the Supreme Court’s review judgment in Vanashakti, questioning whether the recall of the original ruling was driven by principled correction of a per incuriam error or by pragmatic concerns of public interest and economic fallout. It analyses how the Court has consistently struggled with ex post facto environmental clearances, caught between environmental rule of law and socio economic consequences of undoing completed projects. The piece highlights procedural concerns surrounding the use of review as a surrogate appeal, the growing trend of outcome driven adjudication, and the recurring reliance on public interest, fait accompli, and economic waste to dilute environmental safeguards. It argues that the three judge bench missed a crucial opportunity to settle the legality of post facto clearances and instead prolonged uncertainty by restoring a contested regulatory framework. Ultimately, the article contends that the judgment reflects a deeper judicial discomfort in enforcing environmental legality when compliance entails visible economic and infrastructural loss, thereby weakening legal certainty and intergenerational environmental justice.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of the expansion of private insurance coverage for telehealth following the CARES Act (2020) on the earnings of registered nurses (RNs) in the U.S. Using a panel dataset for 21 US states spanning from 2016 to 2023, while employing a difference-in-differences approach to compare the differential hourly wage and annual wage outcomes of registered nurses between states that changed their requirements for private telehealth insurance and those that did not. The results show a significant increase in hourly and annual wages at the 25th percentile for the treated states compared to the control states, while no meaningful results were found at higher wage levels. These findings suggest that the expansion of telehealth not only improved healthcare access but also contributed to improving the welfare of healthcare providers.

detail.abstract: This article argues that the central lesson of Amazon/iRobot is not whether the Commission "got it wrong," but that a salient ex-post shock can expose limits in the analytical framework used to assess dynamic efficiencies in innovative markets as well as the lack of contestability and reflexivity of the EU merger control process. The Commission's Statement of Objections articulated an unusually granular foreclosure mechanism centered on marketplace governance toolsdelisting risk, ranking and labelling, advertising placement, and rivals' advertising costs-treating visibility and trust as inputs into effective market access. That theory may be coherent on the evidence available ex ante, and iRobot's later bankruptcy does not, by itself, falsify it or prove enforcement error. Yet the episode illustrates how merger policy in innovation-intensive sectors can generate socially costly prediction errors when it undervalues merger-based routes to scale, innovate and exit. Because acquisition prospects shape entry and investment incentives, enforcement choices operate as de facto exit policy. The case therefore supports adapting the framework, not the application, to ensure that dynamic efficiencies and incentive effects are evaluated with the same discipline as foreclosure theories, improving the accuracy and legitimacy of merger control. iRobot's ex-post fate also suggests the need for more contestation during and after the merger review process, and more open-minded and reversible remedy design policies.

title: Role of Women's Empowerment in Economic Growth
affiliations: College of Community Science, College of Community Science and Indian Institute of Technology

detail.title: Role of Women's Empowerment in Economic Growth
detail.abstract: Women's empowerment is a fundamental prerequisite for sustainable economic growth and inclusive social development. Ensuring equitable access to education, employment, productive resources, and decision-making authority enables women to function as full economic agents and active contributors to national progress. Empirical evidence underscores this significance: the National Family Health Survey-5 (2019-2021), which covered 724,115 women across 636,699 households in India, highlights the central role of women in shaping household and national outcomes. However, persistent gender disparities remain substantial. Globally, 43.7% of married women lack autonomy in reproductive health decisions, and 35% of women aged 15-49 have experienced physical or sexual violence. Economic empowerment is similarly constrained, with nearly 80% of countries reporting that fewer than half of women possess secure ownership rights to agricultural land. Political underrepresentation further reflects systemic inequality, as women occupy only 27.2% of parliamentary seats worldwide as of 2025. Although 99 legal reforms were enacted between 2019 and 2024 to advance gender equality, structural, socio-cultural, and institutional barriers continue to limit transformative change. Therefore, sustained policy commitment, institutional strengthening, and inclusive development strategies are imperative. Achieving genuine national advancement requires the comprehensive empowerment of women, enabling them to participate equally in economic, social, and political spheres.

title:
The Economic Impacts of Short-term Rentals and Regulations:
A Literature Review
affiliations: and Universidad Complutense de Madrid - GRIPICO

detail.title:
The Economic Impacts of Short-term Rentals and Regulations:
A Literature Review
detail.abstract: This paper provides a systematic review of the literature on the economic impacts of short-term rental (STR) platforms and the regulatory responses they have prompted. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identify 429 papers and synthesize evidence across four domains: housing markets, local economies, tourist accommodation, and neighborhood dynamics. STR constitute a simultaneous multimarket entry that generates efficiency gains alongside distributional consequences and neighborhood externalities. In housing markets, STR raise prices and rents through supply reallocation, with effects strongest in tourism-intensive, supply-constrained areas. In accommodation, STR intensify price competition and generate consumer surplus, particularly during peak demand. Local economies benefit from redirected spending but face compositional change that displaces resident-oriented services. At the neighborhood level, STR increase criminal opportunity and nuisance through transiency. We then assess four regulatory approaches and their effectiveness. A central finding emerges: regulation selects against casual hosts while professionalized operators adapt, explaining why impacts persist after intervention. We distill four evidence-based policy principles for STR governance.

title: Understanding Household Savings in North Sulawesi: A Dynamic Analysis of Rural and Urban Responses to Economic Recovery and Fiscal Austerity
affiliations: Sam Ratulangi University, Sam Ratulangi University, Universiy of Sam Ratulangi, State University of Manado, Sam Ratulangi University and University of Debrecen

detail.title: Understanding Household Savings in North Sulawesi: A Dynamic Analysis of Rural and Urban Responses to Economic Recovery and Fiscal Austerity
detail.abstract: This study investigates the behavior and determinants of household savings in rural and urban areas of North Sulawesi, Indonesia, in the context of ongoing global economic uncertainty and national fiscal tightening. Using a dynamic econometric approach through the Partial Adjustment Model (PAM), the analysis evaluates the influence of real interest rates, Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP), and the productive-age population on savings patterns from 2012 to 2022. The results indicate that GRDP and demographic structure significantly affect household savings in both urban and rural contexts, while the interest rate variable becomes insignificant, particularly during crisis periods. These findings reflect structural challenges in Indonesia's macroeconomic management, where recent austerity measures-though intended to stabilize public finances-have yielded limited impact on economic growth and household welfare. The study underscores the importance of regionally inclusive financial policies, especially in resource-rich yet economically vulnerable areas like North Sulawesi, where dual dependence on mining and agriculture shapes complex household financial behavior. Insights from this research contribute to the broader discourse on financial resilience in emerging economies and the role of householdlevel adjustments in shaping national recovery trajectories.

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, and the Workforce: Evidence from Corporate Executives

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We use novel data from a survey of nearly 750 corporate executives to study the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and the workforce. We document substantial heterogeneity in AI adoption across firms, with more than half having already invested, though many smaller firms are only beginning to do so. Labor productivity gains are positive, vary across sectors, and are expected to strengthen in 2026, with the largest effects concentrated in high-skill services and finance. These gains are not primarily driven by firms' capital deepening but instead reflect increases in revenue-based total factor productivity, closely associated with innovation- and demand-oriented channels. We document a productivity paradox, in which perceived productivity gains are larger than measured productivity gains, likely reflecting a delay in revenue realizations. In labor markets, we find little evidence of near-term aggregate employment declines due to AI, though larger companies anticipate AI-driven workforce reductions, while smaller firms expect modest gains. We also find evidence of compositional reallocation of labor both within and across firms, with routine clerical roles declining and a relative demand for skilled technical roles increasing. We develop an index that ranks job functions most negatively affected by AI.

detail.abstract: In 2025, Russian exports fell to $418.3 bn (-3.7% compared to 2024) amid declining global oil prices. The share of fuel and energy products in Russian exports dropped to 53.9%. Other export groups demonstrated significant recovery growth, most noticeably in the export of machinery and equipment. Imports remained close to previous year and amounted to $279.0 bn (-1.4%), with a decline in the import of investment goods and an increase in the share of consumer goods. China retained its position as Russia's largest trading partner, accounting for approximately 27% of exports and 36% of imports. Shipments of oil, coal, distillates, and LNG to China declined, while pipeline gas and non-ferrous metals exports increased. The discount to Russian oil prices increased at the end of the year. Increased shipments of pharmaceuticals, medical devices and optical instruments from the EU and the US were also observed.
