detail.title: Leakage via Rerouting: Strategic Offsetting and Climate Clubs under Non-CO2 Regulation in Aviation
detail.abstract: We study a model of heterogeneous states' strategic responses to the regulation of non-CO2 effects in (international) aviation. States have two instruments to mitigate those effects: (i) route management (rerouting) and (ii) sustainable aviation fuels (SAF). We characterize equilibrium behavior under three institutional settings: noncooperative competition and two kinds of climate clubs (full and partial cooperation). Total welfare is maximized under full cooperation, when externalities are internalized and leakage-like strategic offsetting by third states is eliminated. Even under partial cooperation, mitigation is insufficient and, more problematically, rerouting can induce less climate-sensitive states to reallocate flights to more climate-damaging routes. This response can weaken the effectiveness of route management and, in the extreme, additional rerouting can even raise global climate harm. In contrast, SAF adoption reduces the scope for strategic offsetting by reducing the need for route management. Despite its positive impact on overall welfare, full cooperation is not necessarily stable due to an unequal internal distribution of mitigation burdens and benefits: Relatively climate-agnostic members may bear mitigation costs without commensurate gains and therefore have incentives to defect, whereas more climate-sensitive members benefit disproportionately from cooperation. These distributional tensions can undermine voluntary cooperation and point to a role for additional club-design instruments (e.g., transfers or burden-sharing rules). Overall, our analysis highlights that effective mitigation of non-CO2 effects requires combining policy instruments (routebased measures and fuel-based abatement) together with institutional mechanisms that limit the gains from opportunism and sustain cooperation.

title: Rest Your Trigger Finger: How Governance Over Illegal Markets Promotes Welfare
affiliations: and

detail.title: Rest Your Trigger Finger: How Governance Over Illegal Markets Promotes Welfare
detail.abstract: This paper examines how the consolidation of criminal governance by the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) reshaped illicit markets and coincided with a sustained decline in homicide in São Paulo beginning in the early 2000s. Drawing on long-term ethnographic research, internal documents seized by law enforcement, and newly assembled city-level data, we argue that the PCC institutionalized governance functions typically associated with the state: monopolizing coercion, providing informal dispute resolution, and regulating drug markets through bureaucratic coordination. We show that the diffusion of these institutions is associated with sharp and demographically concentrated declines in homicide, particularly among young men in peripheral neighborhoods. Using a unique membership registry covering 98 municipalities, we further find that while overall criminal presence correlates with worse outcomes, the allocation of enforcement bureaucrats is associated with lower homicide rates and improved local economic indicators. The findings contribute to debates on informal institutions and development by showing that violence in illegal markets depends on how authority over coercion and economic coordination is structured, rather than on illegality per se.

title: Explaining Cross-Country Heterogeneity in Debt Overhang Thresholds
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), , International Monetary Fund (IMF) and

detail.title: Explaining Cross-Country Heterogeneity in Debt Overhang Thresholds

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper estimates debt overhang thresholds separately for 105 countries using a Kalman Filter approach applied to a standard growth model. The results reveal pronounced heterogeneity in the estimated thresholds, both within and across country groups but limited time-variation. In a second step, we explore the structural factors underlying this heterogeneity. The empirical results underscore that a strong payment track record, high quality institutions and governance, public debt composition (currency, maturity, and creditor base), and financial market size and development are associated with higher pubic debt overhang thresholds.

title: Short-Term Consequences of Parents’ Criminal Legal System Involvement for Children’s Academic Performance
affiliations: Washington University in St-Louis, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Pennsylvania State University and University of Wisconsin-Madison, Institute for Research on Poverty and School of Soical Work

detail.title: Short-Term Consequences of Parents’ Criminal Legal System Involvement for Children’s Academic Performance
detail.abstract: Children from disadvantaged backgrounds disproportionately experience parental criminal legal system (CLS) involvement, potentially hindering their academic achievement. Using linked administrative data from Wisconsin, this study examines the implications of parental CLS involvement for the educational outcomes of 137,938 children ages 7-15 (49% female, 60% White, 13% Black, 16% Other, 11% Hispanic). Using a future treatment comparison group – children whose parents will, but are not currently, involved with CLS – we find that associations between parent CLS involvement and children’s test scores are driven by selection bias. Results from first differences and child-specific fixed effects linear regressions similarly suggest no significant association between parent CLS involvement and children’s test scores. Patterns do not differ when considering parent incarceration versus parent CLS involvement without incarceration. On the whole, this study suggests that children with CLS-involved parents have below-average test scores but parent CLS involvement itself does not worsen children’s educational outcomes.

title: UrbanMorphoSim: A Green Deep Learning Framework for Simulating Air Quality and Socio-economic Benefits of Urban Morphology Transformations in Smart Cities
affiliations: Vietnam National University - Ho Chi Minh City (VNU-HCM) - University of Economics and Law

detail.title: UrbanMorphoSim: A Green Deep Learning Framework for Simulating Air Quality and Socio-economic Benefits of Urban Morphology Transformations in Smart Cities
detail.abstract: Urban air pollution - driven by PM2.5, NO2, and O3 - poses severe public health burdens in rapidly growing cities. Existing deep learning (DL) forecasting models treat air quality as a purely temporal signal, ignoring the static urban morphological context that physically governs pollutant dispersion, while high-fidelity physics-based simulators (e.g., CFD, ENVI-met) remain prohibitively slow for interactive policy use. This study introduces UrbanMorphoSim, a lightweight green DL framework that bridges this gap by fusing hourly multi-pollutant time-series forecasting with an Intervention Embedding mechanism, enabling planners to perform instantaneous what-if simulations of urban morphology changes. A TimesNet_Lite backbone - selected through a rigorous five-seed, two-horizon benchmark against DLinear, CNN-LSTM, and PatchTST_Lite - integrates four morphological proxy variables (Height-to-Width ratio, Vertical Greening, Ground Greening, and Street Orientation) into the forecasting loop. Experiments on a three-year, six-city dataset (2023-2025) yield competitive accuracy (MAE ~9.86, R^2 ~0.765 at the 72-hour horizon). Socio-economic analysis across eight planning scenarios reveals that an Aggressive Eco-City intervention could prevent up to 223 premature deaths and avoid $225.8 M in annual health costs across six cities. Cross-city leave-one-out evaluation confirms strong zero-shot generalisation (mean R^2=0.752), with transfer learning reducing MAE by up to 45% for unseen cities. Monte Carlo analysis further validates robustness under implementation uncertainty. Edge deployment simulations demonstrate sub-millisecond inference at only 0.0025 J per request and 3.07 kg annual CO2e per node, establishing UrbanMorphoSim as a practical, scalable Decision Support System for evidence-based urban planning.

title: Innovative Optimization Studies to Advance the Current State of Isotope Production Target Design at the High Flux Isotope Reactor
affiliations: University of Tennessee, Knoxville, Government of the United States of America - Oak Ridge National Laboratory and University of Tennessee, Knoxville - Department of Nuclear Engineering

detail.title: Innovative Optimization Studies to Advance the Current State of Isotope Production Target Design at the High Flux Isotope Reactor
detail.abstract: A growing demand for various stable and radioactive isotopes is limiting the ability to incorporate new and innovative target designs for isotope production (IP) at the US Department of Energy’s High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) located at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. This demand has increased reliance on historical and conservative approaches, which has forced scientists to operate in a “just-in-time” manner, producing routine yield calculations with few advancements. The goal of this work is to demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of a recently proposed HFIR-specific optimization framework; as a test case, its efficacy is demonstrated for a routinely produced isotope, 188W. The developed framework relies on a Python-based metaheuristic (MH) optimization algorithm coupled with stochastic radiation transport and deterministic activation/depletion/decay codes. The algorithm automatically designs, simulates, and evaluates thousands of unique target design candidates based on user-defined variable ranges, mock input files, and an objective function to maximize 188W production. By using the current target design as the baseline, various new and innovative target designs were found to return higher specific activity (SA), a key radioisotope production metric. The variables explored included the target placement in HFIR, the number of W rings in the target, the option to separate each ring with various spacer materials, and the vertical thicknesses of the rings and spacers. One advantage of this optimization framework is the flexibility and robustness of a newly developed and computationally efficient target design simulation model. Six optimization studies are presented in this article and included nearly 20,000 simulations. These simulations showed that Al-based spacers integrated into a four-ring design increased SA by up to 20% compared with the current eight-ring target design without spacers. Moreover, the MH framework predicted that minimizing the W ring thickness and maximizing spacer thickness would contribute to an even higher SA increase of 31%. Exotic fissile flux-boosting and coproducing spacer materials were also explored, and although they did not outperform the most optimal Al-based spacers, they did contribute to higher SA than the current target design and demonstrated the efficacy of a dual-target system. These results demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed general-use optimization methods for 188W IP target design and indicate much wider applicability for other IP campaigns at HFIR and similar state-of-the-art facilities.

title: Navigating Cross-Pressures: Acculturation and Latino Political Behavior

detail.title: Navigating Cross-Pressures: Acculturation and Latino Political Behavior

declarations.funderStatement: Institute for Latino Studies, University of Notre Dame; National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program

detail.abstract: Latino political behavior has long defied scholarly expectations, producing persistent political diversity that the field's dominant frameworks cannot explain because they were designed to predict collective unity, not individual-level variation. This study introduces the Bidimensional Acculturation Model (BAM) to political science, which treats heritage and American cultural attachments as independent dimensions and identifies four distinct acculturation orientations (culture-affirming, bicultural, demicultural, and assimilationists), and tests whether these orientations produce distinct political profiles using the 2006 Latino National Survey (N = 4,785). The findings confirm that acculturation orientations significantly differentiate ideology, partisanship, and immigration attitudes, with the strongest effects on immigration, and that biculturals, who represent 68% of the sample and are invisible under existing approaches, exhibit a distinct political profile. These results establish psychological acculturation as a theoretically necessary construct for understanding Latino political diversity and offer a framework applicable to immigrant-origin political behavior more broadly.

title: On the Main Determinants of Medical Costs in Accident Insurance: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Swiss Market
affiliations: , Université de Lausanne and University of Lausanne - Department of Actuarial Science (HEC Lausanne)

detail.title: On the Main Determinants of Medical Costs in Accident Insurance: A Comprehensive Analysis of the Swiss Market
detail.abstract: Professional accident insurance (or workers' compensation) covers medical expenses and salary replacement following accidents. Unlike other insurance branches, it operates under a single group policy per company, with premiums varying by company characteristics, region, industry sector, claim history, and other factors. In Switzerland, this insurance is mandatory and divided into two branches: work-related accidents and leisure-time injuries. Using a novel dataset covering the entire Swiss accident insurance market with over 1.5 million companies from 2003 to 2019, we investigate the determinants of medical costs arising from accident insurance claims. This dataset enables, likely for the first time, a direct comparison of work-and leisure-related accidents, the latter of which are rarely examined in the existing literature. Surprisingly, we find that several work-related variables, including company size and industry sector, either directly or indirectly influence medical costs associated with leisure-related accidents. We use regression models to identify and quantify differences across business activities, company sizes and geographical regions.

title: Stablecoins and the Future of Payments

detail.title: Stablecoins and the Future of Payments

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We examine whether financial market participants, in aggregate, expect stablecoins to play an important role in payments. Using high-frequency variation in stock prices, we estimate that U.S. legislation supporting the use of stablecoins in payments reduced the market value of listed incumbent payment firms by 18% or approximately $300 billion, consistent with stablecoins increasing competition in the payments sector. This impact is larger than that of other recent pro-competitive regulatory shocks and (i) proportionately larger for incumbents focused on cross-border payments, (ii) smaller for incumbents protected by network effects, and (iii) smaller for incumbents already offering crypto-related services.

title: Macroeconomic Impacts of EU Defense Spending
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Monetary Fund (IMF), , International Monetary Fund (IMF),  and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Macroeconomic Impacts of EU Defense Spending

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Europe’s defense spending is undergoing a historic shift. With NATO members expected to reach 2% of GDP and discussions underway to increase targets to 5% by 2035, this paper examines the possible macroeconomic consequences of such rearmament using two complementary approaches. First, using an annual panel dataset covering 27 EU countries over the period 1989–2023, we show that past national defense spending has stimulated economic activity in the short term, and entailed sizable cross-border spillovers. Importantly, we find that spending multipliers varied considerably across countries and over time: they tended to be larger when import intensity is low, fiscal space (captured by sovereign yields spread) is ample, and public investment efficiency is high. Second, a novel high-frequency dataset of monthly defense procurement contracts from Opentender, covering EU-27 countries from 2009 to 2023, allows for improved causal identification using fiscal news and instrumental variables based on European aggregate defense procurement and each country’s geographic proximity to major adversaries. The estimates corroborate the positive effects of defense spending on output and show that equipment procurement has the strongest relative impact. Given the larger and more synchronized nature of the current European defense buildup relative to past national episodes in our sample, multipliers might fall below historical estimates, especially if monetary policy is not accommodative.

title: Separating Contingent from Thinking in Strategy-proof Matching Mechanisms *

detail.title: Separating Contingent from Thinking in Strategy-proof Matching Mechanisms *

declarations.ethicsApproval: IRB approval was not obtained for this experiment because, at the time, RWTH Aachen University did not have an IRB for economics experiments.

detail.abstract: We experimentally examine to what extent non-truthtelling in strategy-proof matching mechanisms can be attributed to a failure of contingent thinking (FCT). When we remove the need for applicants to think contingently, we find no increase in truthtelling. If instead, as in the related FCT literature, we inform applicants of contingency probabilities (as opposed to school priorities), removing the need to think contingently increases truthtelling. We conclude that even though applicants exhibit FCT, non-truthtelling in a canonical matching environment with school priorities is not driven by FCT. We conjecture that it is instead caused by non-standard preferences or beliefs.

title: Identification via Heteroskedasticity when Attention is Endogenous

detail.title: Identification via Heteroskedasticity when Attention is Endogenous
detail.abstract: This paper demonstrates that rational inattention can bias structural vector autoregressions identified via heteroskedasticity. Inattentive agents optimally acquire more information during high-volatility regimes, so shock transmission changes with shock variance, which violates the key identifying assumption of constant structural parameters. I characterize the resulting bias and develop two correction methods: one using attention proxies, another exploiting multiple variance regimes. Applying the first of these methods to unconventional monetary policy at the zero lower bound reveals that standard estimates substantially understate the role of expectations in policy transmission, with signalling effects on inflation expectations particularly prominent.

title: Traditional Uzbek Ceremonies and their Impact on the Economy and Households
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Traditional Uzbek Ceremonies and their Impact on the Economy and Households
detail.abstract: This paper examines the economic impact of Uzbek traditional ceremonies, such as circumcisions, weddings and funerals, on the country's economy and household spending behavior. These rituals, deeply rooted in the culture, usually demand significant spending that mostly exceeds an average family's annual income. The study has two main aims: first, to evaluate both macro and microeconomic effects of the related ceremonial expenditures over the past twenty years. Second, it explores the social expectations and governmental regulations that have shaped the financial decision-making of Uzbek households. Findings reveal that traditional ritual parties account for a considerable portion of national expenditure, bringing prosperity to the hospitality, retail and service sectors while burdening households financially, forcing them to incur debt or rely on remittances from labor migration. Although the government has implemented measures to limit excessive spending, these regulations are often ineffective. The study concludes that traditional ceremonies drive household debt and labor migration, thereby reinforcing spending patterns of Uzbek families. For a substantial change, a cultural shift toward modest ceremonies is important to lessen financial and social strain and promote sustainable economic practices.

title: The Psychology of Compliance: Logic Model and Algorithm for An Integrated Regulatory Framework Consisting of Predictive and Risk Rules, Aversion and Certainty Constructs, and Licensing Assessor Bias in Reducing False Positives and Negatives

detail.title: The Psychology of Compliance: Logic Model and Algorithm for An Integrated Regulatory Framework Consisting of Predictive and Risk Rules, Aversion and Certainty Constructs, and Licensing Assessor Bias in Reducing False Positives and Negatives
detail.abstract: The purpose of this short paper is to continue the development of the Integrated Regulatory Framework (IRF)(Fiene, 2026) which should help us establish the parameters of the psychology of compliance within the human care licensing field.  In this paper, a logic model and algorithm will be built consisting of predictive and risk rules taken from the Theory of Regulatory Compliance and Differential Monitoring (Fiene, 2025a), aversion and certainty constructs taken from Prospect Theory (Kahneman & Tversky, 1984), and addressing licensing assessor bias in reducing false positives and negatives (Fiene, 2025b).

title: How does Economic Development Influence Firm Forms? Evidence from the Chinese Accounting Industry
affiliations: Kyoto University

detail.title: How does Economic Development Influence Firm Forms? Evidence from the Chinese Accounting Industry

detail.abstract: This study offers a unique perspective on how economic structures influence firm forms and relevant institutions. It argues that in certain service industries, when residents have higher savings to buffer against risk, businesses are more likely to be organized as partnership firms rather than as limited liability companies. This phenomenon can also influence regulators, leading to the development of formal institutions governing firms. This study validates the argument using data from the Chinese accounting industry. Our results shed light on a field, how contracts and organization forms are chosen, and how institutions are influenced by economic development.

detail.title: On the Origins of Modern East Asia: Knowledge and the Economic Transformation of Japan and China in the late 19th Century

publicationDetails.journalName: Centre for Quantitative History Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper revisits the old thesis of the contrasting paths of modernization between Japan and China. It develops a new analytical framework regarding the role of knowledge acquisition (propositional vs. prescriptive) and political centralization as the key drivers behind these contrasting paths. Our model and historical data highlight how the introduction of these elements contributed to Meiji Japan’s decisive turn towards the West and Qing China’s lethargic response to Western imperialism. Our analytical framework, developed from a comparative historical narrative and quantitative data, sheds new insights onto the importance of knowledge acquisition for enabling developing countries to reach the world’s economic frontier.

title: Automation and Demand-led Growth: Endogenous Wage Elasticity, Macroeconomic Stability, and Policy in the Hicks-Sraffa Supermultiplier
affiliations: Federal University of Goias and Brasilia University (UnB)

detail.title: Automation and Demand-led Growth: Endogenous Wage Elasticity, Macroeconomic Stability, and Policy in the Hicks-Sraffa Supermultiplier

declarations.funderStatement: National Council for Scientific and Technological Development

detail.abstract: This paper extends the Hicks-Sraffa Supermultiplier (HSSM) by endogenising the wage elasticity of labour demand as an increasing function of the investment share, 𝜀 𝐿 (ℎ) = 𝜀 0 + 𝜙ℎ, where 𝜙 > 0 is an automation sensitivity parameter capturing how capital accumulation raises labour-capital substitutability. The modified two-dimensional system yields four results. First, a unique steady state exists in which capacity utilisation converges to its normal level and the investment share is strictly lower than in the exogenous model. Second, the Jacobian determinant is always positive, ruling out saddle-point instability. Third, the endogenous elasticity strengthens stability quantitatively and dampens Harrodian instability, while leaving the qualitative condition 𝛾𝑣 < 𝛼 unchanged. Fourth, at the boundary 𝛾𝑣 = 𝛼 a Hopf bifurcation generates persistent endogenous cycles, with the bifurcation threshold invariant to the automation parameters-so technology policy alone cannot eliminate instability risk. Numerical simulations calibrated to OECD averages confirm all four results. The paper further identifies a stability corridor for the wage elasticity, a double dividend of expansionary fiscal policy, and situates the findings within the Sraffian Supermultiplier tradition, the Bhaduri-Marglin debate, and the mainstream task-based automation literature.

title: A New IV Estimator of a Panel VAR(p) Model
affiliations: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN) and Lund University

detail.title: A New IV Estimator of a Panel VAR(p) Model

declarations.funderStatement: Adrian Mehic acknowledges financial support from the Jan Wallander and Tom Hedelius stiftelse, grant number W23–0009.

publicationDetails.journalName: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We propose a novel dynamic panel estimator. Different from the commonly used difference and system GMM, our proposed estimator requires only one of the crosssectional dimension (N) or the time dimension (T) to grow large to be asymptotically unbiased. This improves reliability in panels with long time spans, where GMM suffers from weak instrument problems, and more generally in finite samples where results can be sensitive to instrument selection and implementation choices. Computationally simple, it extends readily to higher-order autoregressive and vector autoregressive settings. Monte Carlo simulations show that the estimator exhibits lower finite-sample bias than GMM in shorter panels, including for roots at and near unity. In three applications from political economy and macroeconomics-spanning diverse panels, outcomes, and persistence levels-our estimator yields stable, economically meaningful estimates robust to specification choices. By contrast, standard GMM methods display considerable sensitivity to instrument lags, collapsing, and the choice between difference and system variant, often producing substantively different results under comparable setups.

title: Who Pays When Generation Fails? Cross-Border Effects of Swedish Nuclear Outages
affiliations: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN)

detail.title: Who Pays When Generation Fails? Cross-Border Effects of Swedish Nuclear Outages

declarations.funderStatement: The author gratefully acknowledges financial support from the Swedish Energy Agency.

publicationDetails.journalName: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: I estimate the cross-border effects of Swedish nuclear outages using hourly data on day-ahead prices, generation, and consumption across 15 bidding zones in Northern Europe from 2021 to 2024. I exploit unplanned outages as exogenous variation in nuclear supply and find that a 1 GW reduction in Swedish nuclear capacity increases the day-ahead price in the SE-Stockholm bidding zone by approximately 28 percent (17 EUR/MWh). Although less precisely estimated, prices in Finland, Denmark, and the Baltics increase by about 12-13 EUR/MWh. In Norway, contemporaneous price effects are largely offset by increased hydro generation, implying an intertemporal displacement of costs as reservoir levels decline. Since short-run demand is approximately inelastic within the relevant price range, changes in consumer surplus are well approximated by the price change multiplied by the quantity consumed. Abstracting from dynamic effects due to hydro substitution, Swedish consumers bear approximately half of the total short-run loss in consumer surplus, with Finland accounting for the largest share among neighboring countries.

title: Identification of bubble flow patterns of centrifugal pump inlet based on CEEMDAN-FE-LSTM
affiliations: Zhejiang Sci-tech University - Key Laboratory of Fluid Transmission Technology of Zhejiang Province, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Xihua University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Identification of bubble flow patterns of centrifugal pump inlet based on CEEMDAN-FE-LSTM
detail.abstract: Centrifugal pumps operating normally are highly sensitive to gas-liquid mixed transportation. When the gas content exceeds 5%, the gas entrainment at the inlet may lead to a decline in hydraulic performance and even system failure. Traditional gas detection methods present inherent drawbacks in handling time-varying vibration signals. Moreover, they are incapable of accurately capturing time-domain characteristics. To overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, this paper puts forward a new intelligent detection approach. This approach incorporates adaptive noise complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition (CEEMDAN), fuzzy entropy (FE) and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network, termed the CEEMDAN-FE-LSTM model. Specifically, a gas-liquid two-phase flow visualization test bench was constructed. Vibration signals under different flow rates (0.6Qd–1.4Qd) and inlet gas volume fraction were collected, and four flow patterns BF I-IV were identified. The vibration signals were adaptively decomposed into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) by CEEMDAN, and the fuzzy entropy values of each IMF were calculated to construct feature vectors, which were then input into LSTM for flow pattern recognition. The experimental findings indicate that this method achieves a recognition accuracy of 98.33%, and the F1 score also reaches 98.33%. Moreover, this model has high stability, significantly outperforming other comparison models.

title: The Price of Exclusion: Economic Warfare and Market Segmentation under the Continental System
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Price of Exclusion: Economic Warfare and Market Segmentation under the Continental System
detail.abstract: How much does enforced commercial exclusion cost? This paper provides the first systematic quantification of market segmentation under Napoleon's Continental System, one of the most ambitious coordinated attempts at trade-cost escalation. Using a harmonized European commodity price panel spanning seven economies from 1800 to 1820, I apply a triple-difference design that compares imported colonial goods against domestically produced grains across blockaded and non-blockaded economies before and after the 1806 Berlin Decree. Because smuggling circumvented customs ledgers but could not circumvent the risk premia embedded in clandestine routing and overland evasion, equilibrium prices provide a more reliable sufficient statistic for the blockade's economic bite than the fragile quantity series on which prior assessments have relied. The Berlin Decree raised the relative price of colonial imports in blockaded economies by 0.801 log points — equivalent to a 123 percent ad valorem tariff. A formal decomposition of the post-1803 period shows that the war effect is small and statistically indistinguishable from zero, while the blockade effect is large and precisely estimated, directly resolving a longstanding identification problem in the literature. The result ranks first among all 35 possible treatment assignments in exact permutation inference and is stable across all leave-one-out exclusions. The estimated wedge implies a static welfare loss of 0.10 to 0.40 percent of Continental income and raised cotton spinners' marginal production costs by approximately 38 percent. The Continental System imposed a dual distortion: shielding domestic industry from British competition while simultaneously crippling it with unprecedented intermediate input costs.

title: Climate Risk and Financial Stability in Pakistan
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Climate Risk and Financial Stability in Pakistan
detail.abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a systemic financial risk, particularly in climate-vulnerable emerging economies. This paper examines how climaterelated shocks affect financial stability, banking sector risk, and capital allocation in Pakistan. Using macro-financial data, climate disaster indicators, and financial sector exposure measures, the study evaluates whether climate risk is adequately priced within Pakistan's financial system. The findings suggest that climate shocks significantly increase credit risk, sovereign risk, and investment volatility, while existing regulatory frameworks remain insufficient to fully integrate environmental risk into financial decision-making. The paper develops a climate-finance transmission framework and proposes policy measures including climate stress testing, enhanced disclosure standards, and expansion of sustainable finance instruments. The results contribute to the growing literature on climate finance and financial stability in emerging markets.

title: Cross-regional Formal Social Networks: Non-local Chambers of Commerce and the Mobility of Heterogeneous Capital
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and Hefei University of Technology

detail.title: Cross-regional Formal Social Networks: Non-local Chambers of Commerce and the Mobility of Heterogeneous Capital
detail.abstract: Enhancing the spatial allocation of production factors plays a vital role in promoting economic growth, particularly in developing economies. However, whether formal social networks can play a role in this process remains underexplored. Focusing on China, we exploit the establishment of city-level non-local chambers of commerce (NCCs) — a representative form of formal social networks — between 2000 and 2022 as a quasi-natural experiment, applying a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model derived from a structural gravity framework to identify their impact on the cross-regional mobility of heterogeneous capital. We find that the establishment of NCCs significantly promotes capital flows from chambers’ origin cities to their host cities. To address endogeneity, we instrument the establishment of NCCs with historical treaty-port openings during the late Qing dynasty (1840–1910), employ a network-based approach to capture indirect intercity NCClinkages, and control for the effects of the multi-dimensional intercity transportation networks. Mechanism analyses indicate that NCCs enhance capital mobility by reducing institutional transaction costs and alleviating market information frictions, leading to significant heterogeneity across different types of capital. Spatial analyses further reveal that under the influence of NCCs, capital tends to flow from core cities to peripheral ones, exhibiting a pronounced “diffusion” pattern and thereby fostering, to some extent, higher levels of market integration.

title: Cash Crops, Settlement Patterns, and Indigenous Population Growth: The Role of Wine in Colonial Algeria (1900–1950)
affiliations: Universidad de Alcalá, Universitat Barcelona and Charles III University of Madrid

detail.title: Cash Crops, Settlement Patterns, and Indigenous Population Growth: The Role of Wine in Colonial Algeria (1900–1950)
detail.abstract: This paper examines how export-oriented settler agriculture shaped the spatial distribution of indigenous populations in colonial Algeria. By the early twentieth century, Algeria had become one of the world’s largest wine producers and the principal supplier of wine to metropolitan France. We construct a commune-level panel dataset combining census measures of the indigenous population with indicators of viticultural intensity derived from agricultural reports. Exploiting variation in early exposure to viticulture across communes, we show that indigenous population growth became increasingly concentrated in high-viticulture areas from the late 1920s onward, with divergence intensifying during the Great Depression. This pattern is consistent with in-migration driven by the relatively continuous labor demand of viticulture—unlike more seasonal crops—followed by reduced outward mobility as alternative employment opportunities contracted. These findings indicate persistent spatial differences in population growth across communes. This study provides systematic quantitative evidence linking the labor demands of settler monoculture to the spatial concentration of indigenous populations in colonial Algeria.

title: Impact of Bikes on Traffic Efficiency Based on Car-Bike Mixed Traffic Flow Modeling
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Impact of Bikes on Traffic Efficiency Based on Car-Bike Mixed Traffic Flow Modeling
detail.abstract: Bicycles often share low-volume two-way roads with cars, requiring cars to cross the centerline into the opposing lane to pass. When the opposing lane is occupied, cars cannot safely overtake, and bicycles act as moving bottlenecks. The resulting car delay depends on car and bicycle speeds and flows, as well as the interactions of shockwaves and queues, which are difficult to quantify analytically. This study develops a macroscopic car–bike mixed traffic flow model using a numerical solution to the Lax–Hopf equation to quantify the impact of bicycles on traffic flow. A sensitivity analysis examines the effects of average bicycle headway and its variability, bicycle speed and its variability, traffic volumes, and traffic headway variations on delay. Interestingly, results suggest that heterogeneity in car and bicycle flows reduces the influence of queue interactions on delay. Finally, the model compares dedicated bicycle lanes with mixed traffic lanes to evaluate their application domains based on total delay (combined car and bicycle delay). Findings indicate that dedicated bicycle lanes are advantageous across a wide range of conditions, with their effectiveness increasing as the impact on car speed decreases or opposing traffic volumes are lower. The proposed framework provides insights for improving traffic efficiency in environments where cars and bicycles coexist.

title: Beyond the Fit: Assessing Bias-Variance Trade-Off in Johnson-Cook Constitutive Modeling for AA5182
affiliations: Clemson University, Clemson University and Clemson University

detail.title: Beyond the Fit: Assessing Bias-Variance Trade-Off in Johnson-Cook Constitutive Modeling for AA5182
detail.abstract: Physics-based predictive models often contain known inadequacies due to their simplified representation of underlying physical systems, introducing systematic deviations from reality. Despite this, they tend to generalize better than their purely empirical counterparts and are often the only tools available to evaluate or predict the performance of complex engineering systems. In this paper, we present a principled framework for calibrating simulation models with known deficiencies against experimental data and for evaluating their predictive ability. Discussions explore the modeling of a cylindrical AA5182 aluminum alloy specimen tested in compression at temperatures ranging from 200 - 500°C, and at strain rates of 0.001 and 1s-1. A finite element model of the specimen is constructed in Abaqus/CAE 2025 using the Johnson-Cook constitutive model, a common choice for simulating alloy behavior due to its computational efficiency. The Johnson-Cook model has several alloy-specific parameters that must be calibrated against experimental data, introducing uncertainty into the finite element model predictions. Additionally, its simplified treatment of strain hardening leads to systematic discrepancies between simulated and observed material responses, which can be inferred through an independent, empirically trained error function. Herein, we explicitly account for these uncertainties and discrepancies and evaluate the bias-variance trade-off in the model predictions. We propose a metric, Calibration Flexibility Measure, to quantitatively evaluate the trade-off between goodness-of-fit and model complexity. Key decisions, such as selection of calibration parameters, integration of prior knowledge, and definition of model-form error are explored to assess and characterize their effects on posterior distributions and predictive performance.

title: Integrated Optimization of Lane Assignment and Signal Timing for Freeway Ramp-Surface Intersections Based on Flexible Lane-changing Restrictions
affiliations: Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University and Jiangsu University

detail.title: Integrated Optimization of Lane Assignment and Signal Timing for Freeway Ramp-Surface Intersections Based on Flexible Lane-changing Restrictions
detail.abstract: To address the challenges of traffic congestion and illegal continuous lane-changing maneuvers caused by the short distance between freeway ramps and surface intersections, this study proposes an integrated optimization model for lane assignment and signal timing based on flexible lane-changing restrictions. By designating specific segments where lane-changing is permitted or prohibited and utilizing single dashed-solid lines to implement a segregation mechanism, the model provides refined guidance and constraints for weaving behaviors within critical areas. The model is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) framework, aiming to minimize both the system cycle length and the total intensity of weaving conflicts. It comprehensively incorporates constraints regarding signal phase structure, lane-changing behavior, lane configuration, flow equilibrium, and lane capacity, while accounting for drivers' lane-choice tendencies based on the principle of equal queue lengths. To ensure practical applicability, the non-linear components of the objective function are linearized, enabling the model to be solved efficiently using standard optimization solvers. A case study was conducted at a representative section of the Dingmao Elevated Road in Zhenjiang, followed by validation using VISSIM simulation. The results demonstrate that, compared with the Status Quo Scenario, the Proposed Model reduces the average intersection delay by 29.4%, shortens the average queue length by 42.1%, and decreases the total number of traffic conflicts by 54.07%, with a 3.6% reduction in high-risk conflicts. Furthermore, compared with the Rigid Isolation Scenario, the Proposed Model achieves a 15.8% reduction in average delay and a 50.3% decrease in total conflicts. This research confirms that the proposed flexible control strategy offers significant synergistic advantages in enhancing both operational efficiency and traffic safety, providing a novel approach for the design and renovation of complex connection nodes.

title: Wildfire Risk Metric Impact on Public Safety Power Shutoff Cost Savings
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Electric Power Research Institute, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Wildfire Risk Metric Impact on Public Safety Power Shutoff Cost Savings
detail.abstract: Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS) are a proactive strategy to mitigate wildfire risks by preemptively de-energizing power lines and redispatching generation. However, wildfire risk quantification is critical for the operational effectiveness of PSPS. Many existing PSPS formulations rely on the Wildland Fire Potential Index (WFPI) to relate wildfire risk to power system operations. However, this flammability-based wildfire risk correlates less strongly with observed wildfire ignition probabilities (OWIP) than the Large Fire Probability (WLFP). This wildfire modeling discrepancy can distort generation commitments, misinform line de-energizations, and increase real-time (RT) costs. Prior work avoided incorporating wildfire ignition probability (WIP) due to the complexity of modeling wildfire-driven failures as Bernoulli random variables, which introduces non-linear constraints. Leveraging the cross-entropy between WIP and true outages, we represent wildfire risk as the sum of each energized line’s wildfire ignition log probability (log(WIP)), rather than relying on a WFPI proxy. A cross-entropy constraint models joint line failures in a tractable manner without enumerating all failure scenarios. A stochastic day-ahead (DA) unit commitment with the PSPS framework assesses the cost impact of mapping WFPI- or WLFP-based risk metrics to WIP on the IEEE RTS 24-bus and RTS-GMLC systems. Out-of-sample results show that mapping WLFP to log(WIP) in the PSPS optimization leads to more risk-aware decisions and reduces expected and worst-case out-of-sample costs. These findings underscore the benefits of incorporating probabilistic wildfire risk metrics to improve PSPS decision-making for wildfire-resilient power systems.

title: Does Additive Manufacturing Make Firms More Innovative? Evidence on Innovation Quantity and Quality
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Liverpool Management School, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Warwick

detail.title: Does Additive Manufacturing Make Firms More Innovative? Evidence on Innovation Quantity and Quality
detail.abstract: Despite the increasing diffusion of additive manufacturing (AM), little is known about its impact on a firm’s innovation outcomes. This study adopts an exploration–exploitation perspective to examine how AM implementation affects innovation quantity and quality, two important types of innovation outcomes. Using a matched sample of 129 US firms that implemented AM and 129 comparable firms without such implementation over the period of 2011–2019, we employ a difference-in-differences approach to estimate the causal effects of AM implementation on innovation outcomes. The results show that AM implementation has a positive effect on innovation quantity but a negative effect on innovation quality. Further analyses suggest that these effects are contingent on firms’ operational conditions. Specifically, firms with narrower product scope and lower capacity slack experience stronger increases in innovation quantity and less pronounced declines in innovation quality following the AM implementation. Taken together, this study highlights an important trade-off in the innovation consequences of AM implementation and reveals how firms can address this trade-off by adjusting their operational conditions in terms of product scope and capacity slack.

title: EXPORT COMMITMENT AND SUSTAINABLE PERFORMANCE IN MANUFACTURING FIRMS: THE ROLES OF GREEN DYNAMIC CAPABILITY AND INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT
affiliations: Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: EXPORT COMMITMENT AND SUSTAINABLE PERFORMANCE IN MANUFACTURING FIRMS: THE ROLES OF GREEN DYNAMIC CAPABILITY AND INSTITUTIONAL SUPPORT
detail.abstract: This study examines how export commitment contributes to sustainable performance in manufacturing firms, emphasizing the strategic roles of green dynamic capability and institutional support. Drawing on dynamic capability theory and institutional theory, we develop and test a moderated mediation model using cross-sectional, multi-respondent data from 312 export-oriented manufacturing firms in Ghana. Results from partial least squares structural equation modeling show that export commitment positively influences sustainable performance both directly and indirectly through green dynamic capability. Green dynamic capability emerges as a critical strategic mechanism enabling firms to translate export-oriented investments into economic, environmental, and social outcomes. While institutional support does not exert a direct effect on sustainable performance, it significantly strengthens the relationships between export commitment, green dynamic capability, and sustainable performance, thereby amplifying the indirect effect. The findings extend export strategy research by integrating sustainability outcomes and highlighting the contingent role of institutions in emerging economies. Managerially, the study underscores the importance of aligning export strategies with capability development under supportive institutional environments.

title: Reservation scheme for congestion management during morning commute: Considering noncompliance
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Reservation scheme for congestion management during morning commute: Considering noncompliance
detail.abstract: Noncompliance --- the failure of commuters to travel within their reserved time interval --- poses a fundamental challenge to reservation-based travel demand management (TDM) schemes that rely on precise supply--demand matching. We develop an analytical framework for a reservation scheme that systematically conceptualizes and incorporates noncompliance into both scheme design and equilibrium analysis. The authority divides the morning peak into a shoulder--central--shoulder interval structure and distributes quotas accordingly; the noncompliance probability is formulated as a design-sensitive function of the time-interval structure, establishing a principled link between interval design and noncompliance behavior. Three equilibria are derived hierarchically --- the departure time equilibrium (within each interval), the rescheduling equilibrium (across intervals following noncompliance), and the long-term equilibrium (across the implementation cycle) --- and their properties are characterized analytically. Numerical analyses reveal that, while noncompliance generally exacerbates system and travel time costs, this adverse effect can be fully neutralized through appropriate time interval division, which guarantees the proposed scheme's superiority over the laissez-faire case at any noncompliance level. Counterintuitively, noncompliance improves system performance in certain extreme scenarios. Although noncompliance increases total schedule delay costs, the improvement in travel time costs fully offsets this disadvantage, confirming the scheme's overall effectiveness. We provide tailored policy design insights for two distinct managerial objectives: minimizing system cost and ensuring long-term fairness. Furthermore, the analytical insights regarding noncompliance could serve as a methodological reference for broader capacity-constrained reservation systems.

title: Day-Ahead Coordination of Urban Rail Service and Traction Power Supply under Demand-Charge Tariffs and Photovoltaic Uncertainty
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Day-Ahead Coordination of Urban Rail Service and Traction Power Supply under Demand-Charge Tariffs and Photovoltaic Uncertainty

keywords: Urban rail transitTraction power supply system

detail.abstract: Recent research on energy management in urban rail systems has expanded beyond single-train control. When operations integrate timetable scheduling, energy storage, and renewable power, the day-ahead service plan inherently becomes a core component of the power dispatch problem. Minor adjustments to departure times or headways can significantly redistribute traction demand across substations, influence the utilization of regenerative braking, and modify the system's exposure to peak demand charges.,A key characteristic of this joint optimization lies in the structural asymmetry between the two decision layers. Day-ahead service planning is discrete by nature, requiring operators to select from a finite set of feasible operational patterns. Conversely, once a specific pattern is determined, the traction power supply system (TPSS) maintains continuous operational flexibility through grid power exchange, storage management, renewable energy utilization, and regenerative braking absorption. This natural separation motivates a sequential modeling framework where discrete service modes are selected before uncertainties realize, followed by continuous power-side recourse actions.,The presence of demand charges fundamentally alters the evaluation criteria for day-ahead rail operations, as distributing the same total energy consumption across different tariff windows can lead to substantial variations in electricity costs. Therefore, this study investigates the coordination between transport-side service scheduling and the TPSS under photovoltaic uncertainty, explicitly accounting for demand charge mechanisms. By endogenously selecting representative service modes, our approach shapes the baseline traction and regenerative power profiles that the power-side recourse must accommodate. The resulting model is solved exactly utilizing cuts derived directly from the LP recourse value function.,Computational results demonstrate that the primary economic benefit of this coordinated approach stems not from aggregate energy savings, but from the effective flattening of tariff-sensitive grid import peaks. Furthermore, incorporating robust optimization leaves the expected daily cost largely unaffected, while substantially mitigating upper-tail cost risks during periods of renewable energy shortfall, all without causing excessive disruption to passenger service schedules.

title: Red–Blue and Beyond: A Scalable Framework for Airport Access and Intermodal Connectivity
affiliations: Harvard University

detail.title: Red–Blue and Beyond: A Scalable Framework for Airport Access and Intermodal Connectivity
detail.abstract: Metropolitan airports are major trip generators whose ground-access mode shares shape regional congestion, emissions, and equity outcomes. Yet airport access planning frequently underestimates perceived ”transfer penalties” and wayfinding frictions that can make transit itineraries feel unreliable, especially for infrequent travelers and those with luggage. This paper asks how regions can improve airport access by combining long-term intermodal transit investments with near-term operational and wayfinding interventions. Using the Kendall Square–Boston Logan Airport corridor as an applied case, the paper employs qualitative policy analysis and case synthesis drawing from agency plans, publicly available performance indicators, and established research on airport access mode choice, transfer penalties, and wayfinding. Findings support a scalable dual-track framework: network gap closure through fixed-guideway connections, and near-term friction reduction via wayfinding, real-time information, traveler support, and limited-stop shuttle pilots. The framework offers a structured, transferable approach to improving airport access while advancing climate and environmental justice goals.

title: Gig Economy and Corporate Environmental Investments: Evidence from the Ride-hailing Platform
affiliations: School of Economics, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huangshan University, Shanghai International Studies University, School of Business and Management, Shanghai International Studies University and Wenzhou-Kean University

detail.title: Gig Economy and Corporate Environmental Investments: Evidence from the Ride-hailing Platform
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the impact of the gig economy on corporate environmental investments. To better establish causality, we exploit the staggered surge of gig work opportunities induced by the entry of the ride-hailing platform Uber into different cities in China. Using a difference-in-differences approach, we find that the introduction of Uber significantly promotes corporate environmental investments, leading to lower local pollutant emissions. The effect is more pronounced for firms that are more reliant on human capital, and firms in which employees are more exposed to polluted environments. Our findings suggest that the gig economy serves as a catalyst for increased corporate commitment to environmental protection by establishing fallback opportunities for inalienable human capital.

title: Work-Life Integration, Burnout, and Organizational Citizenship Behavior: Their Influence on Employee Performance in the Mining Industry
affiliations: Sam Ratulangi University, Sam Ratulangi University, Sam Ratulangi University, Sam Ratulangi University, Universiy of Sam Ratulangi, Sam Ratulangi University, Sam Ratulangi University and University of Debrecen

detail.title: Work-Life Integration, Burnout, and Organizational Citizenship Behavior: Their Influence on Employee Performance in the Mining Industry
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of work-life integration on employee performance in the mining industry of South Halmahera, with burnout and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) examined as mediating variables. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS), data were collected from 325 employees across production, maintenance, HSSE, logistics, and administrative divisions. The results demonstrate that work-life integration significantly enhances employee performance both directly and indirectly. Work-life integration reduces burnout, promotes higher levels of OCB, and ultimately contributes to improved operational outcomes. Burnout exerts a negative influence on performance, while OCB serves as a strong positive contributor. Both burnout and OCB were found to partially mediate the relationship between work-life integration and employee performance, highlighting the importance of psychological resource preservation and prosocial behavior in demanding and high-risk work environments. This study provides theoretical insight by integrating the Job Demands-Resources Model, Conservation of Resources Theory, and Social Exchange Theory to explain employee outcomes in remote mining settings, and offers practical implications for organizations seeking to enhance productivity, safety compliance, and workforce well-being.

title: Non-Extensive Entropy and Detectability Geometry Under Heavy-Tailed Deformation

detail.title: Non-Extensive Entropy and Detectability Geometry Under Heavy-Tailed Deformation

detail.abstract: Heavy-tailed return distributions and non-Gaussian fluctuations challenge extensive statistical descriptions of financial systems. This study investigates the structural sensitivity of entropy measures under controlled heavy-tail deformation using a truncated symmetric 𝛼-stable framework that interpolates smoothly between Gaussian and heavy-tailed regimes. We first establish local analytical results showing that, in a neighborhood of the Gaussian limit, Tsallis entropy decreases monotonically under tail thickening and exhibits stronger first-order sensitivity to stability-index deformation than Shannon entropy for all 𝑞 > 1. These results provide a theoretical foundation for the subsequent numerical analysis. A standardized separation functional is then constructed to quantify entropy differences between stable and heavy-tailed regimes across a two-parameter space defined by the stability index 𝛼 and the entropic index 𝑞. The resulting response surface is smooth and monotone in both arguments. Detectability regions are characterized through level-set contours, yielding a geometric phase diagram in parameter space. Moderate separation is governed primarily by tail thickness, while strong separation exhibits statistically significant dependence on the entropic index and reflects nonlinear curvature of the response surface. The analysis concerns structural distributional deformation within a synthetic framework rather than empirical forecasting. By combining analytical sensitivity results with phase-diagram geometry, the study provides a coherent interpretation of non-extensive entropy as a structural diagnostic of heavy-tailed stochastic systems.

title: Operator-Decomposed Dynamic Traffic Assignment for Connected Vehicle Corridors under Directional Demand Shocks

detail.title: Operator-Decomposed Dynamic Traffic Assignment for Connected Vehicle Corridors under Directional Demand Shocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Real-time traffic management in connected vehicle corridors becomes particularly challenging when transportation networks are exposed to localized directional demand shocks that generate congestion shockwaves and rapid capacity saturation. Conventional dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) frameworks typically rely on centralized optimization procedures that do not explicitly exploit structural properties of the underlying traffic network, which may lead to unstable routing responses and delayed congestion mitigation under stochastic demand disturbances. This paper introduces an operator-decomposed dynamic traffic assignment framework for connected vehicle corridors subject to directional demand fluctuations. By representing a bidirectional corridor as a network admitting a discrete reflection symmetry, traffic control actions—including routing guidance and variable speed limits—are decomposed into symmetric and antisymmetric components defined by a network symmetry operator. This transformation enables independent control allocation within orthogonal parity subspaces corresponding to corridor-wide congestion dynamics and directional imbalance dynamics. We show that when directional demand disturbances primarily excite the antisymmetric traffic mode, operator-aligned control allocation reduces the spectral amplification of congestion perturbations in the closed-loop system. Consequently, the variance of traffic state fluctuations remains bounded by a constant multiple of the disturbance covariance, implying structural suppression of stochastic congestion amplification. Simulation experiments on a stochastic corridor traffic model demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially improves traffic stability relative to conventional DTA approaches. Peak congestion density is reduced by approximately 18%, average travel time decreases by 16%, and the probability of extreme congestion events is reduced by an order of magnitude. In addition, the operator-decomposed formulation improves numerical conditioning of the control allocation problem, enabling efficient real-time implementation. These results suggest that exploiting structural symmetries in transportation networks provides a powerful mechanism for stabilizing traffic flows in intelligent transportation systems and may serve as a scalable control paradigm for connected vehicle corridors.

title: Entropy-Based Identification of Safe-Haven Regime Shifts in Gold and Silver Markets

detail.title: Entropy-Based Identification of Safe-Haven Regime Shifts in Gold and Silver Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors contributed equally to the conceptualization, methodology, analysis, and writing of the manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: The author(s) received no specific funding for this research.

detail.abstract: Gold and silver are widely regarded as safe-haven assets that provide diversification and hedging benefits during periods of financial stress. However, growing evidence suggests that their safehaven effectiveness is inherently time-varying and may deteriorate during episodes of extreme market pressure. This study develops an entropy-based framework to identify regime shifts in gold and silver markets using Tsallis non-extensive entropy. By tracking the time evolution of the entropic index 𝑞 𝑡 , we detect structural changes in return dynamics associated with transitions from stable safe-haven regimes to periods of heightened co-movement and market fragility. Using calibrated stylized stress simulations and an empirical illustration based on daily GLD and SLV returns, we demonstrate that increases in 𝑞 𝑡 coincide with heavy-tail amplification and distributional reorganization during major stress episodes. The results suggest that entropy-based diagnostics provide a distribution-sensitive complement to conventional correlation-and volatility-based risk measures for monitoring safe-haven stability under non-Gaussian market conditions.

title: Integrating Knowledge Graphs for Hallucination Mitigation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Integrating Knowledge Graphs for Hallucination Mitigation
detail.abstract: This study investigates how integrating knowledge graphs (KGs) into large language model (LLM) inference pipelines mitigates hallucination and enhances trustworthiness. Through a structured comparative evaluation combining retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), ontology-grounded reasoning, and dynamic graph alignment, baseline LLM outputs are compared with KG-integrated systems across medical question answering, geospatial reasoning, and systems engineering modeling. Results demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in hallucination rates, with an average decrease of 31% across evaluated tasks. Effect size analysis indicates substantial mitigation impact (Cohen's d = 1.34) for fully KG-integrated systems relative to baseline. Unexpectedly, graph density and schema rigidity influence reasoning transparency and flexibility differently across domains. The findings suggest that knowledge graph integration strengthens factual grounding and explainability but requires adaptive reasoning structures to avoid over-constraint effects (Hossain; Wagner, Kitzelmann, and Boersch; Lavrinovics et al.).

title: Causal Analysis of Hallucination Triggers in LLM Outputs
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Causal Analysis of Hallucination Triggers in LLM Outputs
detail.abstract: This study investigates the underlying causes of hallucinations in large language model (LLM) outputs, identifying patterns, triggers, and contributing factors. Through experimental evaluation across multiple LLM architectures and input conditions, we identify prompt ambiguity, data sparsity, multi-modal context conflicts, and model overconfidence as primary triggers. Findings indicate that trigger frequency varies by input type and model size, with multi-modal prompts yielding the highest hallucination rates. The study concludes with a taxonomy-driven framework for predicting and mitigating hallucinations in LLM outputs.

title: Governance Architecture and the Protective Mode: A Fourth Governance Type for Mission-Driven Cultural-Religious Organizations

detail.title: Governance Architecture and the Protective Mode: A Fourth Governance Type for Mission-Driven Cultural-Religious Organizations

detail.abstract: Governance scholarship has produced three well-established modes of board governance: fiduciary, strategic, and generative. This paper argues that a fourth mode is both theoretically necessary and empirically demonstrable: the protective mode, governance concerned with the integrity of governance architecture itself. Drawing on the nonprofit board effectiveness literature, Carver's policy governance model and its structural limitations, the higher education mission drift precedent, cooperative ownership theory, and Chait, Ryan, and Taylor's generative governance framework, the paper demonstrates that existing governance theory provides diagnostic and design resources that nonetheless leave a decisive structural gap: the absence of constitutional-choice protections that defend governance architecture itself against capture by actors whose interests diverge from the founding mission. The Protective Mode addresses this gap, operating at Ostrom's constitutionalchoice level to establish structural protections within which fiduciary, strategic, and generative governance can function with confidence that their outcomes will not be overridden. Theologically, the protective mode is grounded in the biblical imperative of shamar: to keep, to guard, to protect what has been entrusted. Paul's charge to Timothy, "keep that which is committed to thy trust" (King James Bible, 1769/2010, 1 Timothy 6:20), names the governance obligation precisely: the parathēkē, the entrusted requires not only faithful stewardship but structural protection adequate to its transmission across generations of leadership.

title: Ethical Implications and Governance Frameworks for Hallucination in LLM Deployment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ethical Implications and Governance Frameworks for Hallucination in LLM Deployment
detail.abstract: This study examines the ethical implications of hallucination in large language model (LLM) deployment and proposes a governance framework for high-stakes applications. Drawing from interdisciplinary research in bioethics, data governance, clinical deployment, and AI policy, the study evaluates how hallucinated outputs affect data integrity, professional accountability, and public trust. Using qualitative policy analysis combined with structured case evaluations in healthcare and software development, the findings reveal that hallucination risk amplifies ethical vulnerability when governance mechanisms are reactive rather than preventive. Unexpectedly, transparency measures alone were insufficient without institutional accountability structures. The study concludes that robust governance requires multi-layered safeguards integrating data stewardship, ethical oversight, auditability, and domain-specific compliance mechanisms. (Hossain; Ghaffar Nia et al.; Hiriyanna and Zhao)

title: Institutional Theory, the Architecture of Capture, and the Governance Protection Gap: Toward Cultural Development Zones

detail.title: Institutional Theory, the Architecture of Capture, and the Governance Protection Gap: Toward Cultural Development Zones

declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper presents theoretical and conceptual analysis drawing on published sources. No human subjects research was conducted in this component of the study.

detail.abstract: Community-based cultural-religious organizations occupy a governance position of structural paradox: the greater the cultural value they produce, the more vulnerable they become to capture by actors whose interests diverge from the founding mission. This paper assembles the intellectual architecture through which this paradox can be analyzed with precision and addressed through deliberate design. Drawing on institutional theory (Weber, Selznick, Michels), the economics of collective action (Stigler, Olson, Hirschman), institutional cognition (Douglas), cultural capital theory (Bourdieu), commons governance (Ostrom), and the macrohistorical analysis of market societies (Polanyi, Fraser), the paper constructs what it terms the governance protection gap: the structural condition in which community-based cultural-religious organizations are systematically more vulnerable to capture than their demonstrated community value warrants. The paper further argues that this gap cannot be closed through individual virtue, democratic aspiration, or legal compliance alone, a claim grounded not only in social science but in the Christian theological tradition through Augustine, Niebuhr, Kuyper, Wolterstorff, and Bonhoeffer. The Cultural Development Zones (CDZ) framework is proposed as the governance architecture that addresses this gap, operating at Ostrom's constitutional-choice level to provide protections that international cultural policy has not yet supplied.

title: Benchmarking Hallucination Across Multimodal Large Language Models

detail.title: Benchmarking Hallucination Across Multimodal Large Language Models
detail.abstract: This study develops a structured benchmarking framework to evaluate hallucination phenomena across multimodal large language models (MLLMs), integrating text, image, and video modalities. Drawing from recent benchmark-driven studies and surveys, the research synthesizes taxonomies, detection strategies, and mitigation techniques to propose a unified evaluation protocol. Findings indicate that hallucination manifests differently across modalities, with video-based models exhibiting higher temporal inconsistency and image-language models showing relational fabrication under ambiguous prompts. The study concludes by proposing a harmonized, taxonomy-driven benchmark that integrates cognitive-inspired categorization and retrieval-based mitigation as core evaluation components.

title: Quantitative Metrics for Hallucination Detection in Generative Models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Quantitative Metrics for Hallucination Detection in Generative Models
detail.abstract: This study develops and systematically evaluates quantitative metrics for detecting hallucinations in generative models, including large language models (LLMs) and multi-modal AI systems. While generative systems demonstrate remarkable fluency and contextual reasoning, they frequently produce hallucinations-outputs that are syntactically coherent yet factually inaccurate or semantically distorted. To address the absence of standardized and scalable detection methods, we comparatively evaluate four quantitative metrics: Factual Consistency Score (FCS), Semantic Divergence (SD), Multi-Modal Coherence (MMC), and confidence-based uncertainty indicators. Experiments are conducted across heterogeneous datasets comprising scientific summaries, news articles, structured reports, and image-text outputs. Results show that metric effectiveness varies by domain and modality. FCS demonstrates strong alignment with expert human judgment in text-centric tasks (r = 0.87), whereas MMC substantially improves detection in multi-modal contexts, reducing misclassification by 18%. Semantic Divergence captures nuanced distortions not identified by surface-level fact matching, while confidence-based indicators reveal calibration-related limitations. A hybrid framework integrating complementary metrics achieves the highest agreement with human evaluators (r = 0.92) and the lowest false positive rate (8%). The findings provide a robust quantitative foundation for reproducible hallucination assessment and reliability benchmarking in generative AI systems.

title: Cross-Lingual Hallucination: Trustworthiness in Multilingual LLMS

detail.title: Cross-Lingual Hallucination: Trustworthiness in Multilingual LLMS
detail.abstract: This study investigates cross-lingual hallucination in multilingual large language models (LLMs) and evaluates their trustworthiness across high-, mid-, and low-resource languages. The research integrates benchmark evaluation, multilingual fact verification, and translation-induced hallucination analysis using datasets such as Poly-FEVER, CChall, and Halluverse-M³. Findings reveal statistically significant disparities in hallucination frequency between English and underrepresented languages, with hallucination rates increasing by up to 27% in low-resource settings. Unexpectedly, cross-lingual knowledge transfer improves factual consistency in some mid-resource languages while degrading reliability in morphologically complex languages. The results demonstrate that multilingual trustworthiness cannot be assumed through scaling alone. We propose structured cross-lingual validation protocols and benchmark diversification as practical mitigation strategies (Hossain; Wu et al.; Islam, Lauscher, and Glavaš).

title: A Governance Framework for Mission Integrity in Community-Based Cultural-Religious Organizations

detail.title: A Governance Framework for Mission Integrity in Community-Based Cultural-Religious Organizations
detail.abstract: This paper presents the Cultural Development Zones (CDZ) framework as the central theoretical contribution of a five-case, four-country governance study of community-based cultural-religious organizations. The study's core empirical finding is that governance architecture, not operational excellence, partnership prestige, or theological commitment alone, determines whether missiondriven organizations survive institutional capture. Seven rival hypotheses were specified a priori and systematically tested against cross-case evidence; six were eliminated and one partially eliminated. The CDZ governance principles thus emerge not from assertion but from the gaps that disciplined falsification reveals, each addressing a specific structural vulnerability and accompanied by a draftable model provision for immediate use by boards, municipalities, and multilateral bodies. The framework operationalizes commitments already articulated in international instruments, the Faro Convention, UNESCO's Culture|2030 Indicators, and the MONDIACULT 2022 Declaration, by supplying the organizational-level architecture those texts imply but do not specify. In doing so, this study seeks to design structures that shield vulnerable communities from extraction, participate in Christ's reconciling work, and embed mission integrity within durable institutional forms.

title: Omega v24.0: A Unified Thermodynamic Framework for Viability, Coherence, and Collapse Across Complex Adaptive Systems

detail.title: Omega v24.0: A Unified Thermodynamic Framework for Viability, Coherence, and Collapse Across Complex Adaptive Systems
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Omega Framework v24.0, a unified thermodynamic model for assessing viability, coherence, and collapse across complex adaptive systems. The framework operationalizes three foundational axioms-energy investment against entropy, critical phase-transition thresholds, and damping-versus-spiraling dynamics-into a 26-construct architecture with a single canonical formula. Building on 60+ domain stress tests across 23 domains and 562 iterative refinements conducted between December 2025 and March 2026, v24.0 introduces twelve architectural innovations including: (1) Pathological vs. Constitutive entropy classification; (2) Agentive vs. Architectural abuse taxonomy; (3) temporal stability vector for multi-timescale crisis detection; (4) Objective Exit Capacity (OEC) for coercive control detection; (5) Construct Applicability Matrix for systematic domain transfer; and (6) non-negotiable safety overrides including a Dead Calm detector. The framework produces three simultaneous outputs-viability diagnosis, ethical evaluation, and structural map-through structural isomorphism across couples, organizations, consciousness, psychotherapy, leadership, and AI systems. A five-phase validation architecture ($370K-$570K, ~20 months) is specified. Empirical validation has not yet been conducted; this paper presents the theoretical architecture and invites collaborative testing.
