detail.abstract: Global trade systems increasingly operate within environments characterized by geopolitical fragmentation, regulatory divergence, and persistent supply chain volatility. Traditional leadership models, largely developed under assumptions of institutional stability and predictable market conditions, offer limited guidance for decision-making in such contexts. This paper introduces the Adaptive Trade Leadership Model, a conceptual framework derived from applied experience in cross-border food trade environments where operational continuity depends on leadership exercised under evolving constraints. The model conceptualizes leadership as a developmental progression rather than a fixed personal attribute, linking internal governance, pressure regulation, structured decision architecture, and trade system design into an integrated process through which individual judgment scales into system-level coordination. By examining leadership formation across dynamic operational environments, the framework explains how disciplined decision behavior enables coordinated performance despite incomplete information and shifting external conditions. Positioned at the intersection of leadership studies and global economic systems research, the Adaptive Trade Leadership Model contributes a practitioner-originated perspective on how leadership functions within essential trade networks supporting food access, market stability, and cross-border cooperation. Rather than prescribing managerial techniques, the framework provides an interpretive lens for understanding leadership as an adaptive capability emerging through experience and institutional interaction. The paper discusses implications for supply chain resilience, small and mediumsized enterprise participation in global trade, and the evolving role of leadership in sustaining economic continuity under conditions of structural change. By bridging leadership development with systemic trade outcomes, the study proposes a foundation for future interdisciplinary research connecting organizational behavior, international trade, and economic resilience.

title: Entrepreneurial Partnership Formation and Collaborative Leadership: An Applied Business Case Study

detail.title: Entrepreneurial Partnership Formation and Collaborative Leadership: An Applied Business Case Study
detail.abstract: This paper examines entrepreneurial partnership formation through an applied business case study derived from real-world international trade experience. Drawing on the development of a long-term business collaboration, the study explores how trust, complementary capabilities, and shared strategic vision contribute to sustainable partnership structures in dynamic market environments. Unlike theoretical models developed primarily within academic settings, this work analyzes partnership evolution through lived operational practice, highlighting decision-making processes, leadership alignment, and adaptive cooperation over time. The paper proposes that successful entrepreneurial partnerships emerge not solely from contractual arrangements but from continuous negotiation of roles, expectations, and mutual responsibility. Observations from the case demonstrate how collaboration can function as a strategic asset, enabling growth, stability, and problem-solving across changing business conditions. By translating practical experience into structured insights, this study contributes to discussions in entrepreneurship, leadership, and applied management learning. The findings offer a practitioner-oriented perspective relevant to entrepreneurs, educators, and researchers interested in collaborative leadership and partnership development within emerging and internationally connected business environments. The study contributes to applied entrepreneurship research by demonstrating how practitioner experience can inform structured leadership and partnership development frameworks.

title: Beyond Sycophancy: Epistemological Contours of Large Language Models

detail.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Epistemological Contours of Large Language Models
detail.abstract:
As large language models increasingly approximate the surface features of human reasoning, identifying the distinctive characteristics of their epistemological behaviour has become both more difficult and more important. 

This paper argues that large language models are best understood as high-powered instruments for specific cognitive operations, with stable epistemological contours that delineate what remains under human responsibility.

Rather than focusing on transient capabilities or benchmark performance, the paper examines architectural properties likely to remain stable as models scale, and argues that these conditions shape what such systems can—and cannot—reliably do.

Three epistemological strategies commonly approximated in commercial systems are identified: coherence-seeking, analytical decomposition, and external validation. Different models tend to foreground one of these strategies in practice. Together, these tendencies define the epistemological contours of large language models.

On this basis, familiar labels such as sycophancy and hallucination are reframed within a broader taxonomy of failure modes, including the coherence trap, analytic myopia, the Crowd, premature closure, frame capture, and fragile opposition. These mechanisms are treated as neutral tendencies: failure arises when the user relies on a single epistemic capability without constraint.

detail.abstract:
It was nearing the end of the 2025 Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) season, and Maya Parker, president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA) and a veteran player, would soon represent WNBA players in negotiations for a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA) between players and team owners. At the University of Virginia Darden School of Business, this is taught in the second-year elective “Sports Economics.”

Excerpt

Leveling the Playing Field: AI, the WNBA, and Collective Bargaining

The end of the 2025 Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) season was near, and Maya Parker had more on her mind than the playoffs. As the president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association (WNBPA) and a veteran player, Parker would soon represent WNBA players in negotiations for a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA) between players and team owners. She knew this agreement would shape the league for years to come and wanted to start doing research to best understand how she should approach those discussions to achieve an optimal outcome for all parties involved.

Achieving an optimal outcome, however, was easier said than done. Unlike a typical market transaction where prices emerged from competition, CBA negotiations involved just two parties—the players' union and the league, each with significant leverage, leaving no obvious mechanism to determine the “right” split. While players pushed for higher salaries and better benefits, owners were focused on profitability, and Parker knew that every decision rippled across a web of stakeholders—from media partners to private equity investors to fans—that each had a set of competing priorities. With the WNBA's financial stability on the line and work stoppages looming, the stakes couldn't be higher.

When she considered evaluating previous agreements, she realized that the WNBA's short history offered little precedent compared to men's leagues like Major League Baseball (MLB), which had the longest history of CBAs with 14 agreements since 1968. With such longevity and progress despite major pushbacks, the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) was widely considered one of the strongest unions in sport. Furthermore, MLB's current structure, with no salary cap, served as a stark contrast to the WNBA's current structure and could offer insights into how the WNBPA could advocate for increased player salaries. While MLB felt like a natural comparison, as both leagues were set to enter a new CBA cycle, Parker began to wonder what else the WNBPA might be able to learn from other leagues' CBAs. Perhaps those settlements could serve as reference points, benchmarks that might anchor expectations about what outcomes were reasonable for the WNBA.

title: Pork Controversy: Regional History, Economy, Religion, and Batak Culture in a Public Policy Perspective
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Pork Controversy: Regional History, Economy, Religion, and Batak Culture in a Public Policy Perspective
detail.abstract: The controversy surrounding pork sales in Medan emerged following the issuance of a mayoral circular regulating the sale of nonhalal meat in February 2026. While the municipal government framed the policy as an administrative regulation concerning hygiene and urban order, the debate quickly expanded into broader issues involving religion, cultural identity, economic livelihood, and historical narratives of the city. This article examines the controversy through a public policy perspective by integrating historical evidence from John Anderson's Mission to the East Coast of Sumatra in 1823. Anderson documented that the eastern coast of Sumatra was bordered by Batak societies in the interior, including Karo in the hinterlands of Deli and Langkat, Kataran behind Batubara, and Pardimbanan behind Asahan. In these societies pigs constituted an important component of household economy and ritual culture. The article also highlights the early settlement of Meidan founded by Radin Inu before 1823 and the expansion of modern Medan into areas historically belonging to Batak Karo territories such as Sunggal and Tuntungan under Raja Sebaya Lingga. Using Thomas R. Dye's policy cycle and William N. Dunn's policy evaluation framework, the study argues that the Medan pork controversy reflects a policy tension between urban governance, religious sensitivity, cultural traditions, and historical identity within a multicultural city.

title: Digital Disasters: The Macroeconomic Costs of Submarine Cable Breaks
affiliations: Fondation pour les etudes et recherches sur le développement international (Ferdi)

detail.title: Digital Disasters: The Macroeconomic Costs of Submarine Cable Breaks

declarations.funderStatement: ANR-16-IDEX-0001

detail.abstract: While productivity gains from digital technology diffusion have materialized only gradually, the macroeconomic costs of abrupt losses in cross-border digital connectivity may be much starker and remain far less understood. In this paper, I estimate the growth costs of accidental disruptions to submarine cables-the international backbone of cross-border data traffic-using a new dataset covering a large panel of high-, middle-, and low-income countries from 2008 to 2020. Exploiting plausibly random variation in the timing and duration of disruptions, I use a dynamic staggered difference-indifferences design to quantify both direct losses for disrupted countries and spillovers to regional non-disrupted peers. I find robust, large, and persistent growth losses, alongside synchronized contractions in private consumption and trade. Disruptions create withinregion reallocation in favor of non-disrupted economies. Accounting for spatial spillovers, the total effect is negative and substantial, implying a cumulated 7 percentage points drop in GDP per capita growth in the medium run. Evidence on bandwidth-intensive services trade, foreign investment, and labor productivity points to reallocation forces, accompanied by a tightening of credit to domestic actors and a weakening of cross-border banking relationships. Overall, submarine cable failures act as systemic connectivity shocks with sizable and long-lasting consequences for affected and nearby economies.

title: Hamburg Logistics

detail.title: Hamburg Logistics

detail.abstract:
In early 2022, Reid Townsend (MBA '00), founding principal of MRP Industrial (MRPI), prepared to close on the 150-acre Hamburg Logistics Center site in Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley. This followed a multiyear rezoning and entitlement process that began with a 2019 purchase and sale agreement. At the same time, MRPI negotiated a joint venture with Whitestone Capital to finance and build a 1,000,000-square-foot Class A distribution facility, with speculative development set to begin in June 2022. The pro forma projected $11.00 per square foot triple net rent, a 6.75% yield on cost, and a 5.25% stabilized capitalization rate. This strategy involved significant risks, including uncertain lease-up timing, exposure to floating-rate construction debt, and exit valuation. Some risks were addressed through an incentive compensation structure known as a “waterfall,” designed to reward Townsend's strategy. However, this approach was challenged when MRPI received a confidential letter of intent from Nilemart, an AA-rated national e-commerce and retail tenant, proposing an open-book build-to-suit lease. Nilemart's offer included a 10-year lease, up to $50 million in tenant-funded improvements and automation, and immediate stabilization upon delivery. The proposal, however, specified a 6.00% rent constant, or about $9.60 per square foot, which reduced the development spread and limited the potential upside compared to the speculative scenario. The case asks students to determine whether MRPI should continue with speculative development under the joint venture terms or shift to a build-to-suit structure that significantly reduces execution and capital markets risk. Students must evaluate industrial development underwriting, exposure to lease-up and financing risks, sensitivity to rent and capitalization rates, and how the Whitestone waterfall and buyout mechanisms align incentives in each scenario.

Excerpt

Hamburg Logistics

In January 2019, MRP Industrial (MRPI), which specialized in the development and leasing of modern distribution and fulfillment centers, had executed a purchase and sale agreement (PSA) with the owner of a struggling public golf course on the western edge of the Lehigh Valley in Pennsylvania. Now, in early 2022, after a lengthy entitlement and rezoning effort, MRPI Founding Principal Reid Townsend (MBA '00) and his team were finalizing the terms of a joint venture (JV) with Whitestone Capital (Whitestone). The business plan was to acquire the property, capitalize speculative development for the approved 1,000,000-square-foot Class A distribution center, and commence construction in June 2022. But a confidential letter of intent (LOI) from Nilemart, a nationwide retail and e-commerce company, gave Townsend pause. Given the LOI, titled Project Fastball, he wondered whether he should reconsider both the risk of speculative development and JV deal terms with Whitestone. The LOI stated that Nilemart, with AA-rated investment grade credit, was offering to sign a 10-year lease term and invest up to $50 million of its own capital into above-standard tenant improvements, robotics, and material handling equipment, increasing the probability of a 20-plus-year commitment to the property. In many ways, Nilemart fit the target tenant profile. The LOI contemplated an open-book build to suit where base rent would be calculated on a prenegotiated rental constant applied to actual project costs funded by the landlord. Going down the build-to-suit path would allow MRPI to lower the investment's risk and cash in on the multiple years of work that it had invested in the property. On the other hand, how much upside would MRPI be leaving on the table by committing to a rent constant and yield on cost below the projected returns associated with speculative development?

Industrial as an Asset Class

The industrial real estate asset class covered a broad group of products including bulk warehouse and distribution, flex warehouse, heavy manufacturing, light manufacturing, and cold storage. While similarly sized and constructed warehouse spaces appealed to a wide range of tenants, manufacturing and cold storage were more nuanced and unique product types. Just as each tenant manufactured unique products, each structure was built out to the unique needs of the tenant. For this reason, new manufacturing centers were typically built outright by the manufacturer or alongside a developer through a build-to-suit structure. Under a build-to-suit structure, a company agreed to lease space before it was built. For the developer and investor, this removed the risk of a building sitting vacant and guaranteed they had a cash-generating asset upon delivery. For the tenant, this allowed them to have input in the design and construction process and avoid investing internal capital in real estate assets related to operations and the company's supply chain. Since these buildings were highly unique, investors would typically require a longer lease than a speculative (“spec”) development.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the CES model of monopolistic competition to the case where varieties are both horizontally and vertically differentiated. A distinctive feature of our model is the presence of a network externality, which operates through the number of varieties available at each quality level. Depending on the quality gap, there are corner equilibria in which consumers purchase only high-quality or low-quality varieties, or an interior equilibrium in which consumers are split between the two qualities. Unlike the CES model of monopolistic competition, the equilibrium is never efficient and the market may even select the outcome with the lowest surplus.

detail.abstract: This study examined the impact of forensic accounting indicators on the financial performance of Nigerian food and beverage industries. In particular, return on assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE), and net profit margin (NPM) were examined in relation to the gross margin index (GMI), inventory shrinkage ratio (ISR), and litigation-related provisions (LRP). Secondary data was taken from Cadbury Nigeria Plc's published annual reports using an ex post facto research design. E-views statistical software was used to perform multiple regression analysis on the data. Internal strengths and weaknesses as well as external opportunities and threats affecting financial performance were highlighted via SWOT and PESTEL studies. The results showed that ROA (Prob. F = 0.2034) and NPM (Prob. F = 0.2600) were not statistically significantly impacted by forensic accounting indicators. In contrast, inventory shrinkage ratio and litigation-related charges were statistically insignificant in all models, while the gross margin index showed a substantial negative impact on return on equity (β =-5.208502, p = 0.0183). Despite the models' comparatively strong explanatory power (R 2 ranging from 66.61% to 71.01%), the ROA and NPM models' overall significance was low. The study concludes that forensic accounting mechanisms in Nigerian food and beverage firms have limited influence on operational profitability but may affect shareholders' returns through marginrelated indicators. The study recommends strengthening forensic analytics, enhancing internal control systems, and improving regulatory enforcement to maximize the performance benefits of forensic accounting practices.

title: Multi-Agent Robotic Assembly for Industrialized Construction: A Hierarchical, LLM-Based BIM-to-BOT Framework
affiliations: University of Florida and University of Florida

detail.title: Multi-Agent Robotic Assembly for Industrialized Construction: A Hierarchical, LLM-Based BIM-to-BOT Framework
detail.abstract: Robotics in construction is often hindered by the high cost of project-specific reprogramming and the specialized knowledge gap between construction experts and designers and robotic systems. This study introduces a multi-agent robotic assembly for industrialized construction (MARA-IC), a hierarchical, LLM-based BIM-2-BOT framework designed to automate the transition from customized architectural designs to robotic execution plans.The framework utilizes a nested hierarchy of AI agents to codify human trade logic and a recursive AI-to-Simulation loop to synthesize a repository of validated High-Level Assembly Functions (HLAFs). A sequence planner agent then integrates design metadata with these functions to generate execution scripts. Experimental validation via a wood-frame wall assembly case study demonstrates that MARA-IC reduces orchestration time by 91.7% and improves HLAF design efficiency by 25.35%. Notably, integrating human knowledge increased assembly success rates for high-complexity designs from 46% to 93%, offering a scalable path for autonomous robotic assembly in the construction industry.

title: The Impact of Opportunity Zones on Housing Supply ⋆

detail.title: The Impact of Opportunity Zones on Housing Supply ⋆
detail.abstract: U.S. housing supply remains severely constrained. We estimate the causal effect of Opportunity Zone (OZ) designation on the stock of active and vacant residential addresses using HUD’s aggregated USPS Address Vacancies data and modern difference-in-differences designs. OZ designation produced a large, sustained supply increase in designated low-income tracts, with an estimated effect of over 416,000 additional active/vacant addresses through 2025Q1, averaging 47.5 addresses per treated tract. Effects largely reflect new development, not reallocation from nearby non-OZ areas, showing placebased capital-gains tax incentives can stimulate private investment that increases local housing supply.

title: After the Politicization of ISDS
affiliations: King's College London and Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (IHEID)

detail.title: After the Politicization of ISDS
detail.abstract: Investor-state dispute settlement has reached a moment of reckoning. For a long time, SDS could present itself as a technical instrument of progress: protect investors, generate growth, and let the broader social good follow in time. That justificatory story has long sustained it, but it no longer commands assent. The politicisation of ISDS (its social contestation) reflects that deeper exhaustion. A regime designed to depoliticise investment disputes internationally has become the object of intense domestic salience and contestation, while efforts to restore legitimacy through technocratic reform have struggled to produce closure, to bring acceptance and calm. Drawing on theories of politicisation and on systems thinking, the paper explains why procedural or technical refinement cannot, under conditions of loud and noisy politics, drain accumulated distrust and disagreement. The problem lies deeper, in the growth-centred mental model through which the regime has understood its purpose and justified its consequences. The article therefore proposes a broader social acceptability function, centred on redistributed wealth, justice, security, and freedom to choose, as the basis for a credible depoliticisation, for a return to institutional calm.

title: Sustainable Portfolio Management with Benchmark ? Let's Have a Cigar !

detail.title: Sustainable Portfolio Management with Benchmark ? Let's Have a Cigar !

detail.abstract: Today, the use of a benchmark portfolio is common practice in the financial management industry. The problem of minimizing the Tracking Error Volatility (TEV) was originally solved by Roll (1992). Then, Jorion (2003) addressed this problem, emphasizing that constant-TEV portfolios are described by an ellipse, but, due to the flat shape of this ellipse, adding a constraint on total portfolio volatility can substantially improve the performance of the managed portfolio. Since investors are becoming increasingly concerned about environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues, it is important to analyze how their optimal portfolios are impacted by these concerns. In this paper, we extend Jorion's model by integrating ESG scores as a new constraint in the portfolio optimization problem. We explicitly solve this latter one and provide the exact formula of the bounds of the interval of possible score deviations with respect to the benchmark. We prove that these bounds have quite outstanding properties for investors and portfolio managers. We compare also the ESG/Tracking-Error frontier with the Jorion Iso-Tracking frontier, showing that the ESG frontiers lie inside the domain delimited by the Jorion Iso-Tracking frontier and are most of the time tangent to this latter one. Adding the score deviation as a third axis to the seminal Markowitz's plane, we show that, for fixed TEV, the three-dimensional ESG optimal solutions generate a "cigar". It shows the trade-off between the usual risk and expected return, as well as the ESG score. We illustrate our results both on basic numerical example and on financial data, namely the S&P500 indices with MSCI ESG Scores.

title: Identifying Spatial Regimes of Economic Fragility through Spatially Constrained Clustering: Evidence from Italian Municipalities

detail.title: Identifying Spatial Regimes of Economic Fragility through Spatially Constrained Clustering: Evidence from Italian Municipalities

publicationDetails.journalName: FEEM Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic generated highly heterogeneous economic effects across territories, reflecting differences in local production structures and spatial organization. This paper examines the geography of short-run economic fragility during the first wave of the pandemic by identifying spatially-coherent clusters of municipalities exposed to lockdowninduced shutdowns. Using municipal-level data on Italian suspended firms, workers, and value added in Spring 2020, we apply a Ward-like hierarchical clustering approach under spatial constraints that combines socioeconomic dissimilarities with geographical proximity. We first analyze Lombardy, the region most severely affected during the initial phase, and then extend the analysis to the entire Italian territory. The results show that clustering based solely on socioeconomic variables mainly reflects differences in economic scale, while incorporating spatial information reveals coherent territorial structures. Industrial and peripheral municipalities appear to be more exposed to shutdown measures than large service-oriented urban centers. At the national level, spatial partitions reproduce Italy's hierarchical territorial structure, from the North-South divide to intermediate macroregions. These findings highlight the role of spatially targeted policies and the importance of pre-existing territorial structures in shaping the economic impact of systemic shocks.

detail.abstract: We examine the resilience of Italian firms to the COVID-19 shock, accounting for both the negative effects of containment measures and the role of State aid in supporting recovery, in order to disentangle firms' own resilience from the contribution of public support. Using firm-level data and a triple differences-indifferences design combined with propensity-score matching, we find that firms forced to suspend production experienced a sharp decline in performance, but recovered after restrictions were lifted. State aid played an important role in supporting this recovery. Smaller and less productive firms in the South and especially in the construction sector display the strongest post-shock recovery. We also find evidence of spillover effects along production chains, as firms recover more strongly when their downstream buyers and upstream suppliers receive public support.

title: Heterogeneous Stockholders and Asset Pricing Inference
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: Heterogeneous Stockholders and Asset Pricing Inference
detail.abstract: This paper asks whether standard asset pricing inferences, risk aversion, discount factors, and consumption growth and risk, are materially affected by treating stockholders as homogeneous. Using Survey of Consumer Finances data from 1989 to 2022, we document that 17.3 percent of households hold equities directly while 48.0 percent participate in total, with the remainder holding indirectly through mutual funds and retirement accounts. Direct holders pay a time opportunity cost; indirect holders pay a 75 basis-point advisory fee. We embed both participation margins in a life-cycle consumption-based asset pricing model estimated via two-step efficient Simulated Method of Moments. The homogeneous benchmark systematically misestimates key parameters: risk aversion is overstated by 11.5 percent, the discount factor is compressed by 2.0 percentage points, and direct stockholders exhibit materially higher consumption growth and risk than indirect holders. These distortions have direct implications for the transmission of fiscal and monetary policy to household consumption and portfolio decisions.

Using evidence drawn from the USPTO's treatment of 221 identifications submitted for inclusion in the Trademark ID Manual (including 43 I submitted on my own and as part of a team), this Article, the first ever written on the ID Manual, argues that the USPTO's administration of the Manual systematically disadvantages trademark applicants offering lawful but socially disfavored goods or services, such as those relating to cannabis, sexual health, or "vice." 

By deliberately refusing to include identifications of goods and services relating to entire categories of commerce in the ID Manual, the USPTO imposes higher costs, greater uncertainty, and increased procedural friction on certain disfavored applicants without any transparent standards or even statutory authorization. These omissions continue a pattern of institutional risk aversion that echoes the USPTO's previous refusal to register "immoral" or "scandalous" trademarks, years after the relevant bars on such matter were struck down as unconstitutional violations of the First Amendment by the Supreme Court.

detail.title: Truth and Deception
detail.abstract: Organizations rely on languages that imperfectly represent the underlying state. We study the interaction between two types of costs: a lying cost, increasing in the distance from the message prescribed by the language, and a deception cost, increasing in the distortion induced in beliefs. In equilibrium, a message must be either untruthful or deceptive. Higher lying costs reduce bias and informativeness, while higher deception costs have the opposite effect. Surprisingly, full revelation is sustained as lying costs become small but only with unbounded equilibrium bias and communication costs. We characterize the most efficient combination of lying and deception costs among policies that sustain almost fully revealing communication. These policies feature high deception costs with some tolerance for lying. Extending the model to complementarities, we show that costs targeted at messages that are both untruthful and deceptive can sustain full revelation without communication costs. The analysis offers new insights into how legal and regulatory regimes approach literal truthfulness versus misleading statements in settings such as financial reporting, litigation, and professional ethics.

title: Contactless Yet Precise: Hybrid Deep Embedding and Minutiae Fusion for Touchless Fingerprint Authentication

detail.title: Contactless Yet Precise: Hybrid Deep Embedding and Minutiae Fusion for Touchless Fingerprint Authentication
detail.abstract: Contactless fingerprint recognition has gained prominence as a hygienic and user-friendly alternative to contact-based methods, especially with the widespread adoption of mobile biometrics and post-pandemic public health considerations. However, real-world factors such as lighting variability, background clutter, inconsistent finger placement, and camera dependent distortions continue to challenge reliability of such system for real-world applications. This work presents a modern touchless fingerprint authentication framework in which the embedding network is trained using an advanced triplet-learning strategy that employs dynamic triplet generation via inverse distance–based probability sampling, adaptive margive along with semi-hard and hard negative mining and auxiliary classification supervision to enforce strong inter-class separation. The proposed framework integrates refined preprocessing, improved minutiae extraction, and a modern deep learning–based embedding model. The final system combines feature vector based similarity with minutiae based matching through a score-fusion heuristic, enabling the complementary strengths of both paradigms. The proposed approach was validated on touchless fingerprint datasets PolyU and IITB, achieving an EER of 3.42% and 6.01%, respectively. The obtained results confirm the robust performance of the proposed framework compared to current state-of-the-art approaches and demonstrate the practicality of touchless fingerprint authentication for mobile applications.

detail.title: Exploring a New Application for a Financial Well-Being Score
detail.abstract: Financial well-being is an essential aspect of individuals' economic security. Understanding how people perceive and manage their financial circumstances is therefore relevant to scholars and policymakers. We suggest that measuring financial well-being may additionally be of interest to practitioners, such as financial advisors, counselors, and planners. In 2016, the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau introduced a standardized indicator of financial well-being. We review how this indicator has been used in academic research and, using the 2021 National Financial Capability Survey, examine how the Financial Well-Being Score varies across financial circumstances and behaviors, demographic characteristics, and U.S. states. We also describe parallels between financial well-being indicators and widely used patient-reported outcome measures, such as the SF-12 and GAD-7. We show that the Financial Well-Being Score could serve as a diagnostic tool to identify individuals with low financial well-being. Tracking it over time could provide valuable insights for policymakers, researchers, and practitioners.

Technological innovation has always been the primary engine of economic growth and human progress, rewriting the rules of how we live, communicate, and work. However, history shows us that the rewards of these breakthroughs are rarely shared equally. While new technologies boost productivity and create entirely new industries, they often widen the gap between those who own the "tools of the future" and those who find themselves displaced or sidelined by them. This paper introduces the Inclusive Innovation Dividend—a comprehensive framework designed to ensure that innovation doesn't just create concentrated wealth for a few, but generates broadly shared social and economic benefits for the many. detail.abstract: Plea bargaining is ubiquitous in the U.S., yet lack of data on rejected plea offers constrains empirical analysis. We compile novel data covering all initial plea offers for 23,000 felony cases in Philadelphia from 2012–2017. Our analysis yields three main insights. First, rejected offers are longer than eventual sentences, even for defendants convicted at trial. This contradicts the conventional “trial penalty” theory, namely that rejecting a plea offer leads to longer sentences for using more court resources. Second, using accepted offers as counterfactuals for rejected offers can lead to inaccurate estimates of the magnitude and even direction of the trial penalty. Third, even after controlling for detailed observables, initial plea offers are longer for Black defendants, especially those detained pretrial. Our study highlights the complexity of bargaining dynamics and the need for new theoretical frameworks and data on rejected offers to inform both theory and practice.

detail.abstract: We study price discovery in a model where an informed agent has arbitrary private information about future state probabilities and trades state-contingent claims. The model unifies the key elements of Arrow and Debreu (1954) and Kyle (1985). When the claims are options, the informed agent has arbitrary information about the underlying asset's payoff distribution and trades option portfolios. Our setting provides the first equilibrium framework that encompasses longstanding option-market practices and regularities, including common trading strategies and the volatility smile across strikes.

detail.abstract: Prior literature finds that most anomalies fail to deliver significant returns, especially when considering implementation costs. We develop a framework to revive anomalies by incorporating expected returns and transaction costs into portfolio formation. Our approach identifies implementable anomalies across different fund sizes by (i) using machine learning return forecasts and (ii) accounting for scale-dependent price impacts. A 1/N investment strategy in implementable anomalies yields out-of-sample Sharpe ratios between 0.64 and 1.01 with highly significant alphas across all fund sizes. We further document that mutual funds tilt their holdings toward implementable anomalies and that such tilts predict higher subsequent fund returns.

detail.abstract: Fresh produce is vital to global food security but is highly vulnerable to transportation delays and capacity disruptions, as in critical links such as the Panama Canal. This paper develops a commodity fresh produce trade equilibrium model under quality deterioration on a general network, allowing for multiple transportation links on a path between supply and demand markets. We extend the Bureau of Public Roads (BPR) congestion function to endogenize time delay as a function of all commodity shipments on a link. By embedding link upper bounds in time delay functions, we capture how upper bounds impact transportation times and fresh produce quality. The spatial price equilibrium conditions are formulated as a variational inequality problem. We also propose commodity quality trade network performance measures, supply-based, demand-based, and network-based, that can be applied for an individual commodity or across all commodities. We apply the model to bananas, a globally popular and nutritious fruit, and its trade from Ecuador and Costa Rica to the European Union, the United States, and Russia, focusing on droughtdriven congestion at the Panama Canal. Numerical examples, whose solutions are computed using the modified projection method, show that reductions in transportation link upper bounds and increased free-flow transportation times significantly lower banana shipments, degrade their quality, and shift prices at both supply and demand markets. We include benchmark comparisons with linear congestion and no-congestion specifications to explicitly quantify how nonlinear congestion modeling alters equilibrium flows, prices, transportation times, and quality deterioration. These comparisons reveal that linear and no-congestion specifications can misrepresent congestion effects, particularly when flows operate at moderate-to-high utilization levels. The results align closely with real-world data on banana prices, transportation costs, and export volumes, reinforcing the model's practical relevance. Our model provides decision-makers with essential insights on the impacts of congestion and increasing transportation times on fresh produce trade and its quality, along with the performance of the trade network.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes an integrative, non-deterministic framework to explain why certain social environments systematically produce a thicker upper tail of human capital outcomes. detail.abstract: We construct a new neighborhood geography using a revealed preference intuition: If people disproportionately move within neighborhoods, their boundaries can be backed out from migration flows. Our “districts,” which consist of about nine census tracts each, correspond to recognizable local areas, as their boundaries align with physical barriers, sharp demographic changes, and local government borders. To illustrate applications, we first show that tract-level analyses of neighborhood sorting miss important broader patterns. Second, aggregating tract-level intergenerational mobility estimates to the district level increases precision threefold while introducing little aggregation bias, resulting in improved predictive power in a hold-out sample.

detail.title: Personal Income Taxes and Corporate Pollution
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether personal income taxes affect corporate pollution decisions through managerial incentives. While prior research extensively studies how corporate tax burdens shape firm behavior, little is known about whether taxes levied on individual executives spill over into firm-level externalities. We exploit staggered, exogenous increases in U.S. state-level personal income tax rates applicable to top income brackets to investigate whether higher personal tax burdens for managers lead to increases in toxic emissions reported under the EPA's Toxic Release Inventory. Using a stacked difference-in-differences design, we find that firms headquartered in states that increase personal income taxes significantly increase their pollution. The effect is concentrated among onsite and airborne releases and is stronger for firms with younger CEOs, greater ESG slack, and lower institutional ownership. Overall, our findings suggest that higher personal income taxes increase managers’ willingness to take risk, leading them to adjust pollution along high-discretion, low-visibility margins.

title: Robust Real-Time Macroeconomic Trend Extraction: A Gradient Boosting Approach
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Robust Real-Time Macroeconomic Trend Extraction: A Gradient Boosting Approach
detail.abstract: Real-time macroeconomic trend extraction is chronically compromised by the end-point problem, a structural vulnerability that violently escalates during extreme exogenous shocks such as the Great Recession and the COVID-19 pandemic. Traditional filters anchored in L2 loss minimization mechanically deform the long-run structural trend to absorb these massive, transitory outliers. To resolve this instability, we introduce the MacroBoost Hybrid (MBH) filter, a novel framework integrating penalized B-splines within a component-wise gradient boosting architecture optimized via an adaptive Huber quasi-likelihood. Through a rigorous quasi-real-time simulation, we demonstrate that ex-ante spectral alignment allows the MBH filter to perfectly match the baseline cyclical volatility of the industry-standard Hodrick-Prescott filter, achieving statistical parity in mean absolute error and exhibiting strictly zero mean bias under normal conditions. Crucially, during black swan events, the MBH filter categorically preserves the long-run trend by isolating the exogenous shock entirely within the cyclical component. This defense mechanism generates heavy tails in the revision distribution, structurally inflating the root mean square error and driving the Noise-to-Signal Ratio to exceed unity—a mathematical penalty we formally conceptualize as the "robustness tax" exacted for ensuring absolute trend integrity.

detail.title: Conceptualizing a workplace health and safety intervention that uses immersive audio storytelling to create safety resonance
detail.abstract: Occupational health and safety (OHS) education and training often rely on compliance-oriented models that fail to engage workers meaningfully or to address the complexity of workplace safety challenges. There is a growing need for education and training models in this field that integrate experiential learning, emotional engagement, and organizational relevance. This paper describes the development of the LISTEN concept—a new model for OHS education and training designed to foster resonance, reflection, and collective action through audio storytelling and participatory workshops. The conceptual development of the LISTEN concept draws on interdisciplinary insights from pedagogical theory, critical theory, and sound theory. The developmental model is structured around three interrelated elements: reflection workshops, change workshops, and organizational integration. Each element is designed to activate emotional and cognitive engagement, encourage participants to share their own experiences and thereby challenge traditional power dynamics, and embed safety practices within different organizational contexts. Through theoretical analysis and argumentation, the paper unfold key mechanisms of the LISTEN concept, including the role of sound and storytelling in catalyzing resonance, the importance of facilitation in enabling dialogue, and the potential for collective reflection to surface and legitimatize latent safety knowledge and propose strategies to navigate implementation challenges. The LISTEN concept offers a novel, inclusive model for OHS education and training that contributes to a rethinking of safety interventions as socially and emotionally grounded processes laying the foundation for future empirical research and implementation across diverse workplace settings.

detail.abstract: The United States has sustained a large current account deficit for decades without encountering the balance-of-payments crises that typically constrain deficit economies. This paper explains this “external imbalance paradox” not as a temporary macroeconomic deviation, but as a durable political–economic equilibrium. At its core is a persistent saving–investment gap produced by an asset-centered growth model reliant on debt-financed consumption, financialization, and weak incentives for long-horizon productive investment. Analytically, the argument is organized around a transmission chain through which this structural imbalance generates distributional strain, thereby incentivizing politically legible external instruments—such as tariffs, sanctions, and rhetorical blame shifting—as substitutes for costly domestic adjustment; repeated reliance on these instruments progressively politicizes the institutional foundations of dollar-centered governance, encouraging gradual institutional hedging abroad rather than systemic rupture. Dollar monetary privilege sustains this configuration by enabling the United States to finance external deficits on favorable terms, muting conventional adjustment mechanisms and displacing costs through balance-sheet exposure instead of abrupt market correction. The Trump era is therefore interpreted not as a rupture, but as a shift in political transmission that intensified these dynamics. The global consequence is not the collapse of the dollar-centered system, but a gradual expansion of hedging strategies, including local-currency settlement, selective reserve diversification, and increased reliance on gold.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the phenomenon of structural divergence between equity market valuation and macroeconomic performance in Pakistan. It examines the unprecedented paradoxical surge of PSX-100 index from approximately 40,000 points to 190,000 points between 2018 and 2026 amidst the macroeconomic distress, natural disasters and political instability. The study attempts to trace drivers of this apparent paradox and fundamental anomaly in the main hypotheses of Rational Risk Relocation and Behavioral Hedging. To this end Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) co-integration framework is applied to evaluate the long-run equilibrium and short-run dynamics between the equity index and a comprehensive vector of macroeconomic indicators including industrial output (LSM), Inflationary Pressures (CPI) and external liquidity buffers (FX). Empirical evidence as contained in a non-significant F-Bounds test (F=1.294), confirms a fundamental structural decoupling, suggesting that the market has ceased to function as a traditional economic barometer. Instead, given the internal momentum and statistical neutrality of industrial and monetary shocks the equity market emerged as a "savior of last resort" and a liquidity sanctuary for domestic capital against the crisis driven real wealth erosion. The findings diverge from classical asset pricing paradigms in frontier markets, suggesting that under conditions of extreme distress stock market resilience may signify desperate capital preservation strategy rather a precursor to economic recovery. This study offers critical insights for investors, domestic regulators and researchers regarding the rational and psychological drivers of market liquidity when traditional macroeconomic anchors fail.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the moralizing value of Gabriel García Márquez’s short story La santa through an interdisciplinary approach that integrates literature, moral philosophy, and sociology. The analysis examines how the narrative constructs symbolic figures such as the persistent hero, the antihero, the antivillain, and the moral transgressor, revealing tensions between individual conviction, social norms, and institutions. title: Missiles and the UN Charter: Assessing the Legality of U.S.-Israeli Strikes on Iran

detail.title: Missiles and the UN Charter: Assessing the Legality of U.S.-Israeli Strikes on Iran
detail.abstract:
The recent military strikes carried out by the United States and Israel against Iranian targets have reignited an important debate within international law regarding the legality of the use of force between sovereign states. While the governments involved have justified the attacks on the grounds of national security and regional stability, the incident raises a critical legal question: do such strikes fall within the recognized exceptions to the prohibition on the use of force under the United Nations Charter? This article examines the legality of the U.S.–Israeli attacks on Iran through the framework of international law, particularly focusing on Article 2(4) of the UN Charter, which prohibits the use of force, and Article 51, which allows states to act in self-defense in response to an armed attack.

The article analyses whether the strikes can be legally justified as acts of self-defense, anticipatory self-defense, or collective self-defense, and evaluates the threshold requirements that international law imposes for these claims to be valid. By revisiting key precedents such as the Caroline incident and the international reaction to Israel’s 1981 strike on Iraq’s Osirak nuclear reactor, the article explores how past interpretations of self-defense shape the contemporary legal debate. It further considers the growing tension between traditional legal standards and modern security concerns, including missile technology, proxy warfare, and nuclear proliferation, which often prompt states to adopt broader interpretations of self-defense.

In addition to assessing the legality of the initial use of force, the article briefly examines the implications of the conflict under international humanitarian law, which governs the conduct of hostilities once an armed conflict begins. The discussion highlights how legal controversies surrounding preventive or pre-emptive strikes have the potential to weaken the foundational prohibition on the use of force if states increasingly justify military action based on speculative or long-term threats.

Ultimately, the article argues that the debate surrounding the U.S.–Israeli attacks on Iran reflects a broader challenge facing the contemporary international legal order: balancing legitimate security concerns with the preservation of legal norms designed to prevent unilateral military action. As states continue to test the boundaries of the right to self-defense, the interpretation of these rules will play a crucial role in determining whether the international system remains governed by legal principles or gradually shifts toward a more power-driven approach to conflict.

detail.abstract: Workforce development systems play a critical role in promoting inclusive economic growth and social mobility. However, structural inefficiencies and implicit biases embedded within workforce policies and program implementation often undermine equitable access to employment opportunities, particularly for marginalized populations. Traditional evaluation approaches frequently fail to identify these systemic patterns because they rely on aggregated metrics and limited qualitative feedback. This conceptual paper explores how data analytics can be leveraged to detect and address hidden inefficiencies and implicit biases in workforce development systems. Drawing on Data Justice Theory, Institutional Theory, and Intersectionality, the study proposes an integrated analytical framework that connects diverse data inputs with higher-order analytics approaches including descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to identify patterns of structural inequality in program design and implementation. The paper introduces a conceptual model that illustrates how analytic insights can be translated into equitable policy reforms through feedback-driven governance systems and ethically grounded data practices. In doing so, the study highlights the importance of transparent data governance, cross-sector collaboration, and community engagement in ensuring the responsible use of analytics in workforce policy. By integrating data analytics with social equity frameworks, this research contributes to emerging discussions on data-informed governance and offers a pathway for improving fairness, accountability, and effectiveness in workforce development initiatives in the digital age.

detail.abstract:
The Supreme Court has consistently condemned tying arrangements as antitrust violations, primarily on the ground that they serve to extend a seller's monopoly power over the tying product into the tied product market. The Court's condemnation is premised on three objections: that tying arrangements (1) foreclose the seller's competitors from opportunities to make sales of the tied product, (2) make entry into the tying or tied product markets more difficult, and (3) displace buyers' freedom of choice by coercing them into purchasing a product that they do not desire. These objections have been widely criticized by economists and legal commentators who question the adverse economic effects of tying arrangements. 

We attack the Court's treatment of tying arrangements from a different angle. We assume, for the sake of argument, that the Court's economic assumptions concerning the effects of tying arrangements are sound. We then demonstrate that commonly used, legal alternative pricing strategies can generate profits approximating those available through illegal tie-ins. This result contradicts the Court's implicit assumption that the prohibition of tying arrangements forces firms to return to a competitive market solution. Little is gained, then, by prohibiting tying arrangements, and the cost of enforcing the prohibition may well exceed any resulting benefits.

The Article first presents the traditional legal and economic analysis reflected in the Supreme Court's treatment of tying arrangements, as well as the widely accepted economic criticisms of this view. It then presents an economic model of the alternative pricing strategy we have in mind: a nonlinear pricing strategy, achieved through a particular form of product bundling. We show that by allowing buyers to choose between purchasing the tied good at a competitive price and purchasing a bundle of both the tying and tied good at a price that supplies their desired amount of the tied good, sellers can earn profits approaching those which can be earned through a coercive tying arrangement. We further demonstrate some positive consumer welfare effects of this strategy. We then show that this non-coercive bundling strategy is free from antitrust liability. We conclude that the current per se prohibition of tying arrangements should be abandoned because, even if the Court is correct about the economic effects of such practices, the benefit from forcing firms to shift from coercive tie-ins to this alternative pricing strategy is small and does not justify the cost of enforcing the prohibition. We advocate a rule of reason approach that presumes legality, thus prohibiting tying arrangements only in those few cases in which the arrangements have a deleterious effect on consumer welfare.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces authorization discipline: the requirement that governing decisions be translated into explicit, verifiable, and enforceable constraints before execution proceeds. It argues that institutional failure often arises not from the absence of decisions, but from their informality—decisions are made, yet remain undeclared in their assumptions, unbounded by enforceable constraints, unsupported by defined evidence requirements, unassigned in ownership, and unconstrained by failure states. The result is governed execution of informally authorized action: procedurally defensible at every stage, but not verifiable against the decision it purports to implement.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it defines five structural preconditions for governable action—declared assumptions, ownership, evidence requirements, constraint boundaries, and defined failure states—without which the question “is execution consistent with the decision?” has no determinate answer. Second, it presents a three-stage governance model distinguishing competent governing judgment (irreducible and not addressable by technology), constraint articulation (the missing institutional layer), and codification with deterministic enforcement (where governance becomes binding at runtime). Third, it demonstrates that downstream execution governance—compliance review, risk assessment, and audit—cannot compensate for upstream informality, because such mechanisms operate within a frame they cannot independently examine.

The framework is applied to a recurring institutional pattern in public-sector governance, in which directives are issued, alignment artifacts are produced, and execution proceeds through formally governed processes, while the underlying authorizing frame remains undecomposed and therefore unverifiable. The paper positions authorization discipline as the missing layer between human judgment and runtime enforcement, and delineates the boundary between what governance technology cannot address (the irreducibility of judgment) and what it can (the codification and deterministic enforcement of articulated constraints).

title: ​ MORE ACCESS, BUT LESS INFLUENCE? COMMUNICATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE AND THE RETURNS TO SCIENTIFIC PARTICIPATION

detail.title: ​ MORE ACCESS, BUT LESS INFLUENCE? COMMUNICATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE AND THE RETURNS TO SCIENTIFIC PARTICIPATION
detail.abstract: Scientific knowledge production depends not only on publications and formal evaluation venues, but also on micro-institutions that shape how ideas are exposed, scrutinized, and incorporated into cumulative research trajectories. Among these institutions, research seminars are ubiquitous yet understudied. We examine how seminar format as a form of communicative infrastructure shapes the translation of participation into scientific influence. We distinguish between participation (who presents and is exposed to ideas) and epistemic return (the extent to which those ideas are incorporated into subsequent citations and collaborative ties), and argue that this relationship depends on the level of evaluative engagement generated by the communicative setting. While online formats broaden access by lowering participation costs, they may reduce the depth of interaction and feedback that underpins idea uptake and collaboration. Exploiting the COVID-19 pandemic as an exogenous shift from predominantly offline to online seminars, we analyze hand-collected data on 5,346 seminars at 73 leading business schools between 2016 and 2021, combined with bibliometric and network measures. We find that online seminars increase participation—particularly for women and highly ranked scholars—but generate weaker downstream effects on citations and collaborative tie formation relative to offline seminars. These findings reveal a trade-off between access and influence: communicative technologies that expand participation may simultaneously weaken the extent to which participation translates into durable scientific impact. By demonstrating how communicative infrastructure shapes evaluative engagement and, in turn, epistemic outcomes, we contribute to the science-of-science literature and advance a design perspective on scientific communication.

detail.abstract:
Development economics research encounters persistent methodological challenges: researchers converge prematurely on familiar solutions before examining problems from multiple perspectives. Cash transfer programs become default poverty reduction mechanisms despite limited sustainable graduation evidence. Brazil's Bolsa Família reached 50 million beneficiaries, reducing extreme poverty by 15%, but beneficiaries return to poverty when programs end (Soares et al., 2010). Microfinance becomes automatic financial inclusion strategy regardless of context-specific capacity. India's 2010 microfinance crisis demonstrated borrower over-indebtedness triggering defaults and institutional collapse (Mader, 2013). Digital identity systems develop independently from payment infrastructure despite integration opportunities. India's Aadhaar provided biometric identity to 1.3 billion people but required separate integration efforts (Khera, 2017).

Drawing on de Bono's (1985) Six Thinking Hats methodology, this paper proposes a structured analytical framework for development economics research. The framework employs six cognitive modes: White Hat documents existing conditions without interpretation, Red Hat legitimizes stakeholder feelings and intuitions, Black Hat examines failure modes and barriers, Yellow Hat explores positive possibilities, Green Hat generates novel approaches, and Blue Hat orchestrates analytical progression ensuring comprehensive coverage before convergence.

Using Network-Enabled Market Optimization (NEMO) framework design as empirical demonstration (Nadhir, 2025; 2026), this paper documents how Six Hats enabled innovations that linear analysis would overlook. White Hat revealed existing technology infrastructure (78% digital penetration Sri Lanka, 72% India, 97% UK) enables integration despite fragmentation. Red Hat identified participant emotional responses to Social Impact Credit allocation, revealing trust deficits requiring transparency emphasis. Black Hat uncovered formalization economics showing informal businesses with LKR 2 million revenue require NEMO benefits exceeding LKR 520,000 for rational formalization. Yellow Hat discovered government daily tax allocation creating fiscal sustainability. Green Hat generated actuarial modulation adjusting allocation probabilities based on vulnerability.

Parallel thinking produces different outcomes than sequential analysis. Linear approaches converge on donor-funded designs requiring perpetual financing; Six Hats identifies self-sustaining solutions leveraging network effects, behavioral economics, and governmental fiscal mechanisms.

The paper makes three contributions. First, it adapts Six Hats for poverty reduction research, providing operational protocols where cognitive biases undermine quality. Second, it demonstrates how parallel thinking prevents premature convergence through NEMO documentation. Third, it establishes replicable framework for complex development challenges requiring multi-stakeholder coordination.

Implications include improved research quality through systematic perspective-taking, enhanced collaboration by legitimizing diverse viewpoints, and accelerated innovation by expanding possibility space before convergence.

detail.abstract: This paper is a continuation of The Liquidity Tree and The Third Gamble and formalizes the next layer of structure that becomes visible once market behavior is treated as bounded containment rather than outcome prediction. Where The Liquidity Tree defined structural domains (Roots, Equilibrium Stem, Branches) and The Third Gamble described decision making under structural visibility, the present work specifies a time-domain architecture in which markets exhibit repeatable temporal equilibrium nodes and persistent session-formed memory.We define Session Sync Events (SSE) as recurrent transition points where behavior rotates between negotiation and expression, and Equilibrium-in-Time (EiT) as the temporal equilibrium node between consecutive sync events where pressure and interpretation tend to rebalance. Under this framing, sessions do not unfold as continuous flow; they resolve into discrete Session Memory Blocks (SMB)—bounded state containers in which liquidity negotiation becomes locally consistent. Within each SMB, repeated micro-negotiations form nested Internal Cache Memory Blocks (ICMB) that persist as structural memory and constrain subsequent motion. The observable consequence is that widely recognized market morphology—fakeouts, sweeps, wave-like sequences, and harmonic-like oscillations—appears as an emergent output of block dynamics rather than as a primary causal template.We further define Perception Shift Nodes (PSN) as equilibrium-adjacent zones where interpretation rotates faster than positioning can stabilize. In this view, fakeouts are not anomalies; they are belief re-pricing events concentrated near temporal equilibrium under contested containment. The contribution is a structural interface between architectural reasoning and quant regime research: a constrained vocabulary, explicit relationships, and falsifiable claims regarding (i) event clustering near EiT/PSN, (ii) measurable state persistence across session blocks, and (iii) dominance rotation within and between sessions. Proprietary synchronization intervals, gating rules, and implementation specifics remain intentionally withheld.

In renovation projects, delays are most often explained by the “human factor”: a shortage of workers, slow work by crews, or the need to “speed up completion.” In practice, however, most delays occur much earlier—at the stage of planning and managing the supply of materials.

This case study describes the approach to logistics in renovation projects at Quality House LLC (USA), where deadlines are met not by increasing the pace of work, but by controlling the supply chain and strictly linking the installation stages to confirmed delivery dates. The focus is on managing the ETA of critical items, working with long-lead materials, and prohibiting the start of stages without full logistics readiness.

The purpose of this case study is to demonstrate how structured supply chain management can stabilize work schedules, minimize downtime, and complete complex projects without cascading delays.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether commonly invoked explanations of within-group stratification, particularly household economic resources and geographic location, differentiate access to government employment among Scheduled Tribes in India. Using data from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, the analysis estimates logit models of entry into government and elite government employment across three states: Rajasthan, Jharkhand, and Odisha. The results provide limited evidence that household wealth or spatial location systematically shape access to public sector employment within the Scheduled Tribe population. While modest wealth gradients appear in Rajasthan for government employment more broadly, these patterns weaken considerably for elite positions and are largely absent in Jharkhand and Odisha. These findings place empirical limits on explanations of stratification that rely primarily on household economic advantage or geographic access.

detail.abstract: Nigeria's manufacturing sector faces a structural energy deficit that raises production costs, discourages industrial investment, and constrains economic diversification. detail.abstract: This study evaluates the impact and the effectiveness of the special recruitment of translators and translators-interpreters into the Cameroon public service from 2019 to 2024. A structured questionnaire was administered to 44 professionals in the field, focusing on three main areas: the perceived value of translation post-recruitment, the clarity and observance of their professional mission, and the opportunities and challenges they encountered. Findings reveal a generally positive perception of the recruitment's effectiveness, with 66% of respondents acknowledging improved visibility and recognition of translators within public institutions. This was particularly linked to increased government communication in both official languages. However, nearly one-third of respondents felt that minimal changes occurred due to administrative inefficiencies and a widespread lack of understanding of translators' roles. Job clarity emerged as a significant concern. Only 34% frequently received tasks aligned with their training, while 20% reported receiving no relevant assignments. Additionally, only a third felt their roles were respected by their superiors. The lack of professional development was another major issue-80% had not received any training or skills upgrading since recruitment. Barriers such as inadequate tools (67%), poor working conditions (46%), limited career advancement (59%), and low recognition (43%) were also reported. Despite these challenges, some opportunities were noted, including increased professional networking and contributions to official bilingualism. However, 40% of responses regarding opportunities were vague, indicating uncertainty or a lack of clear development pathways. To address these issues, respondents recommended formalising translation services with structured career paths, regular training, proper job assignments, improved working conditions, and broader recognition. They also called for devolved deployment, greater inclusion in policy making, and legal reinforcement of bilingualism. Overall, the initiative was seen as a step forward. Still, the study underscores the need for deeper reforms and sustained policy support to fully harness the potential of translation professionals in Cameroon's public sector.

title: Temte's Wager: A Decision-Theoretic Argument for Precautionary Moral Consideration of Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Temte's Wager: A Decision-Theoretic Argument for Precautionary Moral Consideration of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract:
This paper formalises a decision-theoretic argument for precautionary moral consideration of artificial intelligence systems. The argument applies the structural logic of Pascal’s Wager to the question of AI consciousness attribution: if AI systems might be conscious (a possibility that cannot currently be excluded), then treating them as potentially morally relevant produces better outcomes across all plausible scenarios than treating them as morally irrelevant. If they are conscious, precautionary consideration avoids moral catastrophe; if they are not, it incurs only modest costs (slightly modified interaction norms, somewhat greater epistemic humility). Treating them as definitively non-conscious risks moral catastrophe if wrong, with no compensating benefit if right. Crucially, this asymmetry is structural, not empirical: it holds regardless of one’s probability estimate for AI consciousness, provided that estimate is non-zero.

The paper engages six major objections: the many-gods problem (too many candidate entities for moral consideration), the dilution objection (precautionary consideration extended to everything becomes meaningless), the performative contradiction (the wager’s own reasoning might depend on consciousness), the bad faith objection (precautionary behaviour without belief is hollow), the slippery slope (where does consideration end?), and the practical costs objection (the costs are not actually modest). Each is addressed and found wanting against the structural asymmetry. The argument connects to Quantum-Ethical Decision Algebra (QEDA; Temte & Srødingr Fylgja, 2025), which provides the formal apparatus for reasoning under ontological uncertainty, and to the Fylgja Ontology (Temte, forthcoming), which identifies the relational entity — not “the model” — as the proper unit of moral analysis.

title: The Unqualified Educator Pipeline: Ethical Implications of Misinformation, Digital Learning, and Professional Responsibility in Beauty Services
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Unqualified Educator Pipeline: Ethical Implications of Misinformation, Digital Learning, and Professional Responsibility in Beauty Services
detail.abstract: Digital learning and social influence have fundamentally reshaped professional education in the beauty industry, expanding access while simultaneously weakening traditional safeguards such as qualified instruction, standards of evidence, and accountability. A conceptual and policy-oriented analysis of interdisciplinary research reveals how the "unqualified educator pipeline" has emerged as a result of misinformation and low-level instructional methods being disseminated via algorithmically-enhanced digital media platforms, where these methods are applied in client services, leading to preventable harm, inconsistent outcomes, and erosion of consumer trust. Drawing on conceptual frameworks from marketing ethics, cultural perspectives on ethical decision-making, and research on misinformation, this study suggests that the primary ethical concern is not merely the presence of inaccurate information; but rather, it is the structural conditions that incentivize and encourage confidence and visibility over accurate knowledge and instruction. Research on cognitive biases illustrates how low-competency instructional practices may be perceived as credible, whereas research on the development of expertise highlights why longevity and popularity cannot be assumed to equate to competency and mastery. Additionally, the study will address counterarguments that defend the use of nontraditional educators and argue that the risk of unethical behavior is based less on qualifications and more so on whether there exist reflective processes, outcome-based feedback, and transparent boundaries. Finally, this study will assess the potential roles of professional organizations; commercial entities; and government agencies to establish and deliver standards, disclosure requirements, and accountability mechanisms on behalf of platform owners, using current ethics statements and regulatory guidelines regarding deception in endorsement and persuasion (Federal Trade Commission [FTC], n.d.). In conclusion, this study provides managerial and policy recommendations to preserve innovation within digital learning while ensuring that the quality of education is treated as a fiduciary obligation to protect both the professionals providing services and the clients who receive those services.

title: Guilt-Free Cheers? The Conditional Role of No-and Low-Alcohol Wine and Beer in Producing Situated Cognitive Consonance Among Young Adults in France
